articles.title: Added Value of Preoperative Contrast Enhanced Mammography in Staging of Malignant Breast Lesions (PROCEM): A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: Background Contrast-enhanced mammography (CEM) is increasingly used in breast cancer diagnostics; however, randomized trials assessing the added value of CEM in preoperative staging of breast cancer beyond digital mammography, digital breast tomosynthesis, and US are lacking. Purpose To assess the added value of CEM for preoperative breast cancer staging in a randomized controlled trial. Materials and Methods This prospective randomized controlled trial (Added Value of Preoperative Contrast Enhanced Mammography in Staging of Malignant Breast Lesions) enrolled women diagnosed with early-stage breast cancer eligible for primary surgery at two breast centers in Sweden. Participants were randomized 1:1 to preoperative CEM or control from November 2020 through April 2024. The primary outcome was a 10% change in treatment due to preoperative CEM findings. Secondary outcomes included differences in reoperation and mastectomy rates between groups and accuracy of malignant extent estimation with CEM, mammography/tomosynthesis, and US using histopathologic extent as the reference, assessed with Bland-Altman statistics and concordance analysis. Subgroup analyses were performed according to menopausal status, breast density, histopathologic type of cancer, lesion size, and presence of microcalcifications at baseline imaging. Results In total, 415 participants (median age, 66 years; IQR, 56-73 years) completed the trial: 202 in the CEM group and 213 in the control group. Treatment was changed in 17 of 202 participants (8.4%; 95% CI: 5.3, 13.1) based on CEM findings. No evidence of differences was observed between the CEM and control groups with regard to mastectomy (17% [35 of 202] vs 18% [39 of 213]; P = .78) or reoperation (7.9% [16 of 202] vs 10% [22 of 213]; P = .39) rates. CEM showed the closest agreement with histopathologic malignant extent (bias, 3.5 mm), outperforming mammography and/or tomosynthesis (4.8 mm) and US (10.7 mm) overall and in nine of 10 predefined subgroups, except for ductal carcinoma in situ. Conclusion This trial did not meet its primary end point of a 10% treatment change; however, preoperative CEM improved malignant extent estimation. See also the editorial by Mesurolle and El Khoury in this issue.

articles.title: ESR Essentials: MRI of the scrotum-practice recommendations by the European Society of Urogenital Radiology.
articles.abstract: While conventional ultrasonography (US) remains the first-line imaging modality for scrotal pathology, multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) has emerged as a valuable problem-solving tool for indeterminate US findings. Owing to its superior soft-tissue contrast, functional imaging capabilities, and operator independence, mpMRI allows for the precise localization and characterization of scrotal lesions. This paper from the European Society of Urogenital Radiology Scrotal and Penile Imaging Working Group provides a comprehensive, evidence-based overview of scrotal mpMRI for a general radiologist. It details optimized imaging protocols, recommending a standard sequence of T1-weighted, T2-weighted, diffusion-weighted, and subtracted dynamic contrast-enhanced imaging. The article highlights key clinical indications, including the characterization of intratesticular and paratesticular masses, local staging of testicular germ cell tumors, and differentiation between germ cell and sex cord-stromal neoplasms. This paper familiarizes radiologists with normal MRI appearances and MRI findings of common scrotal diseases. Evidence-based recommendations for reporting basic MRI examinations of the scrotum are also provided. The potential of advanced techniques, such as diffusion tensor imaging and proton MR spectroscopy, and the future integration of artificial intelligence and radiomics, are also discussed. We hope the implementation of these recommendations into radiological practice will enhance diagnostic confidence and promote standardized practice in scrotal MRI for radiologists. KEY POINTS: While conventional ultrasound is the first-line modality for scrotal pathology, it can yield inconclusive findings regarding complex mass characterization and local tumor staging. Multiparametric MRI combines anatomical and functional data to accurately characterize scrotal masses, localize impalpable, undescended testes, and provide precise local tumor staging. Scrotal multiparametric MRI serves as a valuable problem-solving tool that enhances diagnostic confidence in sonographically indeterminate cases, prevents unnecessary radical orchiectomies, supports testis-sparing surgery or active surveillance, and standardizes radiological reporting templates to optimize personalized patient management.

articles.title: Development of an Electronic Clinical Quality Measure for Excessive Radiation Dose or Inadequate Image Quality in Diagnostic CT in Adults.
articles.abstract: The Excessive Radiation Dose or Inadequate Image Quality for Diagnostic CT in Adults (ExRad) measure is the first automated radiology outcome measure adopted by CMS. We describe its development, specification, calculation, and adoption. Beginning in 2018, the measure was developed under a CMS cooperative agreement following the Measures Management System Blueprint, with oversight from a multidisciplinary Technical Expert Panel. ExRad evaluates each adult diagnostic CT examination in three steps. First, the examination is assigned to 1 of 19 CT categories defined by anatomic region and clinical indication using International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Clinical Modification and Current Procedural Terminology codes. Second, size-adjusted radiation dose and image noise are computed from the DICOM dose report and pixel data; because clinical and radiology data reside in separate systems, translation software inside the hospital firewall performs the linkage and calculations automatically. Third, dose and noise are compared with category-specific thresholds derived from a reader study in which 125 radiologists rated the image quality of 734 CT examinations. An examination is out of range if either value exceeds its threshold, and the measure score is the percentage of eligible examinations that are out of range. Testing across 32 facilities in eight health systems confirmed the availability, accuracy, validity, and reproducibility of all data elements, and the National Quality Forum endorsed the measure in 2021. CMS adopted ExRad in 2023 into hospital inpatient, hospital outpatient, and clinician quality reporting programs, with voluntary reporting beginning in 2025. It is the sole outcome measure in the Diagnostic Radiology MIPS (Merit-Based Incentive Payment System) Value Pathway.

articles.title: The mismatch between PRISMA and AMSTAR-2: Does adherence to one standard set authors up to fail another?
articles.abstract: The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement and AMSTAR-2 are widely used to support the reporting and methodological appraisal of systematic reviews, respectively. Although conceptually complementary, the frameworks are not fully aligned. Consequently, reviews that adhere closely to PRISMA 2020 may receive low AMSTAR-2 confidence ratings. Five recent PRISMA-compliant meta-analyses published in European Radiology illustrate this disconnect: all were rated as having "low" AMSTAR-2 confidence as they failed to provide a detailed list and justification of excluded studies and to report the funding sources of included studies, requirements emphasised by AMSTAR-2 but not formulated as equivalent standalone requirements in PRISMA 2020. Similar patterns have been reported in other clinical fields, suggesting structural misalignment rather than uniformly poor methodological quality. The discrepancy is amplified by AMSTAR-2's designation of critical domains, whereby a single unmet critical item can substantially lower the overall confidence rating, as well as by ambiguity in interpreting certain criteria. Although AMSTAR-2 was intended to support contextual methodological appraisal rather than simple scoring, it is frequently applied as a rigid checklist. Better alignment could include more graduated AMSTAR-2 judgements, clearer appraisal guidance, and incorporation into PRISMA of selected methodological elements emphasised by AMSTAR-2. Ultimately, journals, reviewers, and authors should distinguish reporting completeness from methodological quality and apply both frameworks thoughtfully, transparently, and with appropriate contextual judgement. KEY POINTS: Question Why can PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic reviews receive low AMSTAR-2 confidence ratings? Findings There is structural misalignment between AMSTAR-2 and PRISMA 2020 requirements, and failure to meet a single critical item in AMSTAR-2 can substantially lower the overall rating. Clinical relevance Better alignment between the frameworks and more context-sensitive appraisal are needed to avoid misleading assessments of systematic reviews.

articles.title: Learning to fuse and reconstruct multi-view graphs for diabetic retinopathy grading.
articles.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is one of the leading causes of vision loss worldwide, making early and accurate DR grading critical for timely intervention. Recent clinical practices leverage multi-view fundus images for DR detection with a wide coverage of the field of view (FOV), motivating deep learning methods to explore the potential of multi-view learning for DR grading. However, existing methods often overlook the inter-view correlations when fusing multi-view fundus images, failing to fully exploit the inherent consistency across views originating from the same patient. In this work, we present MVGFDR, an end-to-end Multi-View Graph Fusion framework for DR grading. Different from existing methods that directly fuse visual features from multiple views, MVGFDR is equipped with a novel Multi-View Graph Fusion (MVGF) module to explicitly disentangle the shared and view-specific visual features. Specifically, MVGF comprises three key components: ① Multi-view Graph Initialization, which constructs visual graphs via residual-guided connections and employs Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) coefficients as frequency-domain anchors; ② Multi-view Graph Fusion, which integrates selective nodes across multi-view graphs based on frequency-domain relevance to capture complementary view-specific information; and ③ Masked Cross-view Reconstruction, which leverages masked reconstruction of shared information across views to facilitate view-invariant representation learning. Extensive experimental results on MFIDDR, by far the largest multi-view fundus image dataset, demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art overall performance for diabetic retinopathy grading. Code is available at https://github.com/HaoranLi525/MVGFDR.

articles.title: KAMP-Net: Knowledge-aligned Multi-modal Prompt-tuning Network for Prostate Cancer Diagnosis from bpMRI.
articles.abstract: Bi-parametric magnetic resonance imaging (bpMRI) is widely used for non-invasive diagnosis of clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa). Although the Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) standardizes interpretation through structured diagnostic criteria, clinical assessment remains highly operator-dependent. Vision-language models (VLMs), such as CLIP, offer a promising automated solution by leveraging the imaging-language coupling inherent in PI-RADS. However, existing VLM adaptation methods generally treat medical diagnosis as a generic image-to-label matching task. This conventional "label-driven" paradigm relies on superficial semantic correlations, fundamentally failing to capture the structured reasoning, anatomical context, and sequence prioritization defined by clinical guidelines like PI-RADS. To address this fundamental limitation, we propose KAMP-Net, a multi-modal prompt-tuning network that shifts the paradigm toward "knowledge-driven" learning. Our core algorithmic novelty lies in mathematically translating structured PI-RADS criteria directly into the network's computational graph. Specifically, rather than employing generic feature fusion and global alignment, KAMP-Net utilizes zone-aware modality routing to dynamically gate heterogeneous bpMRI sequences, and enforces a hierarchical vision-language alignment that structurally mirrors a radiologist's bottom-up diagnostic workflow. Experiments on a multi-center cohort comprising two public and one private datasets, plus an external private dataset, show that KAMP-Net delivers competitive performance in both patient-level diagnosis and lesion-level localization. Beyond standalone performance, we evaluated its clinical utility in an AI-assisted workflow. Notably, for challenging equivocal cases (PI-RADS = 3), this human-in-the-loop strategy successfully reduces false positives without risking missed diagnoses, demonstrating its strong potential as a reliable decision-support tool. Code is available at: https://github.com/IsYuchenYuan/KAMP-Net.

articles.title: Voxelwise white-matter compositional connectivity mapping from diffusion MRI via reliability-aware hierarchical inference.
articles.abstract: Diffusion MRI tractography enables non-invasive mapping of brain connectivity but is commonly summarized as region-to-region graphs, obscuring the fine-grained organization of white-matter pathways. Voxelwise connection distribution maps (CDMs) preserve this information by representing the relative distribution of tractography-derived connections to anatomical targets at each voxel. However, normalized streamline-count profiles are noisy estimates of latent streamline-target compositions, and existing approaches neither quantify their uncertainty nor use population information to stabilize individual estimates. We propose individualized connection distribution mapping (iCDM), which extends CDM through an isometric log-ratio (ILR) representation, hierarchical empirical-Bayes inference of latent individual compositions, and quantification of inferential uncertainty and individual-population support. Individual streamline counts define the likelihood, while a spatially varying population prior is estimated from group data; its precision reflects between-subject dispersion, and its mean can be conditioned on independently learned subject characteristics. Simulations showed lower estimation error than naive and Dirichlet-multinomial estimates, with additional benefit from characteristic-conditioned priors when the characteristic explained substantial variation. Compositions remained similar under within-tractogram split-half sampling and tested changes in seeding and streamline budget. In independent scan-rescan data, data-information maps were reproducible, and greater data information was associated with lower compositional divergence. In a pediatric cohort, iCDM detected age-related compositional variation at voxel and tract levels. In tumor patients, posterior support shifted from predominantly population-based in lesion cores toward greater individual-data support with distance from the lesion. iCDM provides uncertainty-aware voxelwise connectivity inference for population-level and individualized analyses in basic and clinical research.

articles.title: Anatomical prior-guided implicit segmentation of challenging thin and tubular anatomical structures in CBCT images.
articles.abstract: Medical image segmentation has achieved promising performance with deep learning approaches like nnU-Net. However, extremely precise segmentation of challenging topological structures, particularly thin anatomical structures, remains an unsolved problem. In digital dentistry, cortical bone in the mandible and maxillary regions and the inferior alveolar nerve (IAN) represent such thin structures and tubular topologies, where accurate segmentation from Cone-beam Computed Tomography (CBCT) scans is crucial for treatment planning. To address this challenge, we propose an anatomy-guided coarse-to-fine framework. After an initial coarse CNN-based stage, we apply an implicit refinement function to enhance segmentation, focusing on uncertain regions through point-wise selection. To guide this refinement, we leverage the Signed Distance Field (SDF) of teeth as an anatomical prior, exploiting their stable spatial relationship with the target structures. Extensive evaluations on challenging dental CBCT datasets, including both cortical bone and IAN segmentation, demonstrate our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods across metrics. In particular, it achieves over 30% improvements in distance error metrics (ASD and HD). These results validate its robustness and generalization for precise thin structure segmentation in dental CBCT images. Our code is available at https://github.com/ShanghaiTech-IMPACT/Anatomical-Prior-guided-Implicit-Segmentation-of-Thin-Anatomical-Structures-in-CBCT-image.

articles.title: Reducing operator-dependent variability in liver shear wave elastography through an AI-guided region-of-interest placement pipeline.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To develop and evaluate an artificial intelligence (AI) pipeline that automates optimal circular region-of-interest (ROI) placement and the surrounding elastogram box, provides probe-angle/contact guidance, and measures skin-to-capsule distance (SCD) to standardize liver SWE acquisition, aiming to reduce operator-dependent variability. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A two-stage pipeline combined SimCLR self-supervised pretraining on 17,441 unlabeled ultrasound images, followed by ENet fine-tuning using 495 annotated images for liver segmentation and 1564 images for poor probe contact detection. Segmentation outputs were combined with constraints on valid liver tissue pixels, axial depth, lateral boundaries, and regions of poor acoustic coupling to generate masks for optimal ROI placement. A distance transformation algorithm then identified optimal ROI coordinates within these masks. An inter-observer reader study assessed AI performance by comparing automated ROI placement, SCD measurements, and probe-angle correction guidance with annotations from expert attending radiologists. RESULTS: 18,182 US images from 654 liver elastography examinations in 609 patients (mean age, 52.6 ± 12.95 years; 55.4% male) were acquired from three ultrasound systems. The AI pipeline achieved liver segmentation performance with a Dice coefficient of 0.89, sensitivity of 0.95, specificity of 0.93, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.94. The reader study demonstrated significantly higher AI-to-attending radiologist agreement (93.8%) compared to inter-attending agreement for ROI placement (81%). Cohen's kappa agreement between two attending radiologists was 0.25. CONCLUSION: The proposed AI-driven pipeline significantly improved ROI placement consistency and reproducibility, highlighting its potential to enhance clinical reliability in liver fibrosis assessment. KEY POINTS: Question Operator-dependent variability in region-of-interest (ROI) placement compromises measurement reproducibility in B-mode shear wave elastography. We developed an AI pipeline to place an optimal ROI. Findings The AI pipeline achieved liver segmentation performance of Dice 0.89 (AUC 0.94) and demonstrated higher AI-to-attending agreement (93.8%) than inter-attending agreement (81%) for ROI placement. Clinical relevance By standardizing ROI placement, elastogram box selection, and probe angle/contact guidance, the AI pipeline reduces operator-dependent variability in liver SWE acquisition, supporting more reproducible liver stiffness measurements that could improve fibrosis staging reliability.

articles.title: An integrated MRI-pathology model for predicting response to TACE combined with targeted therapy and immunotherapy in hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: The efficacy of transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) plus targeted therapy and immunotherapy in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is limited by variable responses. We aimed to develop and validate an integrated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-pathology model for response prediction and survival stratification (IMPRESS), which combines pretreatment MRI habitat radiomics and paired biopsy whole-slide images (WSIs) pathomics. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter, retrospective study enrolled patients with unresectable HCC receiving TACE plus targeted therapy and immunotherapy from January 2019 to December 2024. Eligibility required pretreatment MRI and paired biopsy WSIs within 1 month before therapy, Child-Pugh class A/B, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status ≤ 1, and at least one measurable intrahepatic lesion ≥ 1 cm. Patients with missing or poor-quality MRI or WSIs, prior locoregional or systemic HCC therapy, second malignancy, ECOG ≥ 2, or incomplete data were excluded. Habitat MRI radiomics, WSI pathomics, and clinical features were integrated into IMPRESS. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Single-cell analysis was performed to explore the biological basis of the IMPRESS predictions. RESULTS: Among 231 patients, 94 (40.7%) achieved a treatment response. IMPRESS achieved AUCs of 0.957 (95% CI: 0.931-1.0), 0.878 (95% CI: 0.789-0.966), and 0.875 (95% CI: 0.782-0.966) in the training, validation, and test cohorts, respectively. Predicted responders and non-responders showed significantly different overall survival in all cohorts (all p < 0.001). Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed distinct immune and proliferative patterns consistent with model predictions. CONCLUSION: IMPRESS model may provide a promising tool for pretreatment response prediction and survival risk stratification in unresectable HCC undergoing TACE-based combination therapy. KEY POINTS: Question Reliable pretreatment tools are needed to identify unresectable HCC patients likely to benefit from TACE plus targeted therapy and immunotherapy. Findings An integrated MRI-pathology model combining habitat radiomics and deep-learning pathomics predicted treatment response, with validation and testing areas under the curve of 0.878 and 0.875. Clinical relevance The integrated model may support pretreatment response stratification for TACE-based triple therapy and help inform surveillance intensity or alternative treatment considerations, pending prospective validation.

articles.title: A fractal-integrated CT score predicts high-risk pathology and early recurrence in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop and validate a noninvasive CT-based imaging score incorporating fractal analysis to predict high-risk pathological features in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and to assess its prognostic value for early recurrence. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective bicenter study included 514 patients with pathologically confirmed PDAC who underwent curative resection, divided into training (n = 219), internal validation (n = 94), external validation (n = 100) and outcome datasets (n = 101). The fractal dimension (FD) and lacunarity were extracted from portal venous-phase CT images via box-counting algorithms. Imaging predictors of high-risk pathological features, including high tumor grade, lymphovascular invasion (LVI) and perineural invasion (PNI), were identified by logistic regression and integrated into a comprehensive weighted imaging score. Cox regression analyses were performed to assess its prognostic value for early recurrence. RESULTS: Patients with high-risk pathological features exhibited greater FD and lacunarity. The final score included six imaging features: necrosis, peripancreatic fat infiltration, venous involvement, regional lymphadenopathy, FD and lacunarity. For any high-risk pathology, the fractal-integrated score achieved AUC of 0.94, 0.88 and 0.84 in the training, internal validation and external validation datasets, respectively. For high pathological burden, the AUCs were 0.92, 0.80, and 0.77. In the outcome dataset, the score was an independent predictor of early recurrence (HR = 2.71; p = 0.004) and improved prognostic discrimination when combined with pathologic predictors. CONCLUSION: This CT-based score, integrating fractal biomarkers, enables accurate, noninvasive preoperative prediction of aggressive pathological features in PDAC and provides incremental value for early recurrence risk stratification. KEY POINTS: Question Can the fractal-based imaging features be used to predict high-risk pathological features and guide risk stratification for early recurrence in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC)? Findings This CT-based score integrating fractal analysis predicted high-risk pathological features and was independent predictors of early recurrence and provided incremental prognostic value beyond pathologic factors. Clinical relevance This CT-based imaging score may help identify patients at high-risk of aggressive pathology before surgery and may further complement postoperative pathological risk stratification for early recurrence.

articles.title: Early Implementation Performance of the CMS Electronic Clinical Quality Measure for Excessive Radiation Dose or Inadequate Image Quality in Diagnostic CT: An Evaluation of 254 Facilities.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate early facility performance on the CMS-adopted Excessive Radiation Dose or Inadequate Image Quality for Diagnostic CT in Adults (ExRad) measure, the first automated radiology outcome measure in CMS payment programs, during the first 16 months of the measure's inclusion in CMS programs. METHODS: ExRad evaluates each adult diagnostic CT examination in three steps: assignment to 1 of 19 CT categories defined by anatomic region and clinical indication; computation of size-adjusted radiation dose and image noise from the DICOM radiation dose-structured report and pixel data; and comparison of both against category-specific thresholds. Because the clinical and radiology data sit in separate systems, translation software inside the health system firewall may be used to perform the linkage. An examination is out of range if its dose or noise exceeds its category threshold; a facility's score is the percentage of eligible examinations out of range (lower is better). We analyzed all facilities reporting between May 2025 and August 2026. RESULTS: Across 254 facilities and 783,634 examinations in 16 CT categories, 30.7% were out of range: 240,409 (30.7%) exceeded the dose threshold and 446 (0.06%) the noise threshold. Facility scores varied widely: median 29.5% (interquartile range [IQR] 18.4-44.7; range 1.8-82.4), with facilities at the 90th percentile scoring 4.6 times more out-of-range scans than those at the 10th percentile. Median out-of-range percentages by category ranged from 0% (routine and low-dose cardiac) to 82.6% (high-dose head; IQR 23.5-100.0); routine abdomen and pelvis, the highest-volume category, had a median of 43.9% (IQR 30.1-61.3). Within facilities, the median gap between best- and worst-performing category was 74 percentage points (IQR 49-89; intraclass correlation coefficient = 0.12). DISCUSSION: Early ExRad performance varied widely across facilities and across CT categories within the same facility. Most variation reflected particular facility-category combinations, so facilities need their own category-level results to identify which protocols to target.

articles.title: Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence Readiness: Building Artificial Intelligence Acumen for Tomorrow's Workforce.
Phase 2 Trial of 89Zr-Deferoxamine-Daratumumab for CD38-targeted Immuno-PET/CT Detection of Multiple Myeloma.
articles.abstract: Background Multiple myeloma (MM) imaging is currently suboptimal, which may limit patient care. Zirconium 89 (89Zr) deferoxamine (DFO)-daratumumab is a novel CD38-targeted immuno-PET tracer. Purpose To compare 89Zr-DFO-daratumumab PET/CT against standard-of-care fluorine 18 (18F) fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET/CT for detection of MM. Materials and Methods Participants with MM were accrued to this prospective phase 2 trial between March 2022 and July 2025. Standard-of-care 18F-FDG PET/CT and bone marrow biopsy were performed, along with research 89Zr-DFO-daratumumab PET/CT. If there were discrepant lesions between the two scans, image-guided biopsy was considered as the reference standard. The McNemar test was used to compare disease detection between the two imaging modalities. Results This study included 60 participants (median age, 63 years [IQR, 57-71 years]; 32 women). 89Zr-DFO-daratumumab PET/CT demonstrated at least one positive lesion in 43% (26 of 60; 95% CI: 31, 57) of participants, and 18F-FDG PET/CT demonstrated at least one positive lesion in 47% (28 of 60; 95% CI: 33, 60) of participants. While there was no overall difference in disease detection between the two imaging modalities (P = .81), MM was demonstrated only with 89Zr-DFO-daratumumab PET/CT in 13% (eight of 60) of participants, with subsequent biopsy confirmation of active myeloma. Conclusion In participants with MM, CD38-targeted 89Zr-DFO-daratumumab immuno-PET helped detect active myeloma in some participants with no signs of disease at 18F-FDG PET/CT. Clinical trial registration no. NCT04814615 © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Choyke in this issue.

articles.title: 2026 RSNA Outstanding Researcher.
Predicting Lymph Node Metastasis in Part-Solid Lung Adenocarcinomas with a Maximum Solid Portion Diameter of 30.0 mm.
articles.abstract: Background The incidence of lymph node (LN) metastasis in patients with part-solid nodules (PSNs) is known to be low, which makes the intraoperative evaluation of LNs a controversial issue. Purpose To investigate the incidence of LN metastasis and explore clinical-radiologic predicting factors for LN metastasis in PSN lung adenocarcinomas with a solid portion diameter of 30.0 mm or less in a large surgical study sample. Materials and Methods This retrospective study included patients with part-solid lung adenocarcinomas with solid portion diameters of 30.0 mm or less on preoperative CT images from July 2023 to December 2024. For each PSN, overall tumor size, solid portion diameter, consolidation-to-tumor ratio (CTR), location, margin, shape, spiculation, lobulation, pleural retraction, bubble-like lucency, and air bronchogram were independently evaluated by two chest radiologists blinded to clinical information and pathology results. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve, calibration, and decision curve analysis. Results This study included 1444 patients (median age, 59 years; IQR, 51-67 years; 931 women). The frequency of LN metastasis was 4.7% (68 of 1444 patients). None of the 115 patients with a CTR of 0.25 or less had LN metastasis (N1: 0 of 115; N2: 0 of 115). Rarely (0.2%, one of 552), LN metastasis was found in patients with a solid portion diameter of 6.0 mm or less. Solid portion diameter was the only independent predictor of LN metastasis (odds ratio, 1.25; 95% CI: 1.20, 1.31) in multivariable analysis and showed a superior diagnostic performance compared with CTR (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.86 [95% CI: 0.82, 0.90] vs 0.75 [95% CI: 0.68, 0.80]; P < .001), along with better calibration (Brier score, 0.039 vs 0.044) and greater net benefit. The clinical actionable cutoff for solid portion diameter was 7.3 mm (sensitivity, 95.6%; specificity, 49.6%). Conclusion Solid portion diameter had a superior diagnostic performance compared with CTR in predicting LN metastasis in patients with part-solid lung adenocarcinomas of solid portion diameter of 30.0 mm or less at CT. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article.

articles.title: Long-Term Comparison of US-guided Microwave Ablation Combined with Ethanol Injection versus Surgery for Nodular Retrosternal Goiter.
articles.abstract: Background Microwave ablation (MWA) combined with ethanol injection (EI) is a minimally invasive technique under preliminary investigation for the treatment of nodular retrosternal goiter (RSG) and has shown promising treatment efficacy. However, a comparative analysis between ablation and surgery is warranted to draw definitive conclusions. Purpose To compare the long-term efficacy and safety of MWA combined with EI versus surgery for patients with nodular RSG. Materials and Methods This retrospective study included patients with nodular RSG treated with MWA combined with EI or surgery between October 2016 and June 2024. Propensity score matching was performed for patients in the ablation and surgery groups, followed by comparisons between the two groups with independent-sample t test, Mann-Whitney U test, χ2, or Fisher exact test. Primary outcomes were treatment success, symptom score, and complication rate. Secondary outcomes were cosmetic score, hospitalization, procedure time, estimated blood loss, incision length, and cost. Results This study included 555 patients (mean age ± SD, 51 years ± 14.4; 414 women). After propensity score matching, 224 patients in the ablation group and 224 patients in the surgery group were observed for a median of 48 months (IQR, 24-60 months). No evidence of a difference was observed in the treatment success rates between the ablation and surgery group (98.7% [221 of 224] vs 100% [224 of 224], respectively; P = .08), while both modalities effectively lowered symptom scores from baseline (both P < .001). Compared with surgery, MWA resulted in a lower complication rate (2.2% [five of 224] vs 34.8% [78 of 224], P < .001), shorter posttreatment hospitalization (P < .001), shorter procedure time (P < .001), reduced estimated blood loss (P < .001), shorter incision length (P < .001), lower cost (P < .001), and lower cosmetic score (mean, 1.1 ± 0.3 vs 1.2 ± 0.4; P = .03) at the 12-month follow-up. Conclusion MWA combined with EI was as effective as surgery for nodular RSGs, providing comparable symptom relief while demonstrating fewer complications, offering a safer alternative for eligible patients. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article.

articles.title: Mapping Gadolinium-based Contrast Agent Residues in the Rat Kidney.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Gadolinium-based contrast agents (GBCAs) are routinely used to enhance magnetic resonance (MR) imaging. In recent years, GBCA residues were detected in multiple organs, with the kidney as the primary organ of excretion showing the highest concentrations. This study aimed to map the intricate spatial distribution of GBCA residues in rat kidneys at an early and a late time point. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Rats received one of 6 marketed GBCAs [3 macrocyclic, 3 linear; cumulative dose 4.8 mmol gadolinium (Gd)/kg] or saline and were sacrificed at day 5 or week 14 post administration (n = 5 per GBCA and time point). In whole renal tissue slices, the distribution of elemental Gd was determined by laser ablation-inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry and the distribution of intact GBCA chelates by matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization-mass spectrometry imaging. In ex vivo kidneys, MR relaxometry was used to assess MR-detectable GBCA residues. RESULTS: At day 5, Gd was predominantly localized in the renal cortex across all GBCAs, with 10- to 100-fold lower medullary levels. Distribution patterns corresponded well with those of exemplary intact GBCA chelates. At week 14, Gd levels had decreased by 1 to 2 orders of magnitude. Distribution patterns from linear GBCAs showed Gd remaining predominantly in the cortex, while Gd from macrocyclic GBCAs was similar in cortex and medulla. Several GBCAs exhibited a prominent Gd presence at the transition zone between outer and inner medulla. Intact chelate was only detectable for the exemplary macrocyclic GBCA, with a spatial distribution pattern matching that of elemental Gd. MR relaxometry detected GBCA residues within ex vivo kidneys but also in the surrounding water-based fixative. This indicated the presence and washout of intact GBCAs, which was greater for macrocyclic versus linear GBCAs. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides the first comprehensive spatially resolved characterization of renal GBCA residues at an early and a late time point. GBCA residues exhibited specific intrarenal distribution patterns and distinct changes in these patterns over the course of their elimination. Our findings of specific retention patterns suggest that renal microanatomy and local physicochemical conditions play critical roles in GBCA retention. These insights provide a foundation for future investigations into retention mechanisms and potential long-term tissue effects.

articles.title: Radiomics performance to identify high-risk carotid artery plaques: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Stroke is a leading cause of mortality worldwide, with 15-20% of ischemic strokes caused by extracranial carotid atherosclerotic disease. Risk stratification has traditionally relied on luminal stenosis severity, which inadequately reflects plaque vulnerability. Radiomics offers an emerging solution by extracting high-dimensional quantitative data from standard medical images. This systematic review evaluated the performance of radiomics-based models for identifying high-risk carotid plaques. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across multiple databases. Studies were included if they developed or validated radiomics-based models for carotid plaque assessment and reported performance metrics, specifically the area under the curve (AUC). Data were extracted on study design, imaging modalities, segmentation methods, and modeling techniques. RESULTS: Twenty-eight studies involving 6,108 patients (72.4% male) were included. Computed tomography angiography was the most commonly used imaging modality (n = 16), and manual region-of-interest segmentation was performed in 27 of 28 studies. Radiomics models showed strong predictive performance. Internal validation AUCs were as high as 0.984, whereas combined models incorporating radiomics with clinical and/or conventional radiological features achieved the best predictive accuracy, often exceeding 0.90. However, only four studies included external validation cohorts. CONCLUSION: Radiomics is a powerful, non-invasive tool for identifying high-risk carotid plaques, offering superior discriminative power over conventional stenosis-based assessments. Despite these promising results, the field faces significant hurdles, and future research must prioritize prospective multicenter trials, the development of automated segmentation workflows, and the correlation of radiomic features with histopathological findings to ensure clinical reproducibility and transition into routine stroke prevention. KEY POINTS: Question Standard carotid atherosclerotic disease assessments fail to capture biological plaque complexity and vulnerability, necessitating objective, reproducible, and non-invasive methods to improve stroke prevention. Findings Radiomics and combined models demonstrate superior capability in identifying high-risk carotid plaques compared to traditional assessments. With four external validations, the field remains exploratory. Relevance statement Radiomics offers a non-invasive tool for personalized stroke prevention. However, technical barriers currently prevent its transition to routine clinical use, including reliance on manual segmentation and low compliance with international standardization guidelines.

Per-Channel Complex  B 1 +   Mapping for Parallel Transmit Ultra-High Field MRI.
articles.abstract: Ultra-high field (UHF, B0 ≥ 7 T) MRI provides substantial gains in signal-to-noise ratio, spatial resolution and contrast. Routine clinical deployment has been limited by challenges of transmit field (  B 1 +   ) inhomogeneity and specific absorption rate (SAR). Parallel transmission (pTx) can mitigate these challenges but it requires per-channel complex  B 1 +   maps to design effective pTx pulses. We review established and emerging approaches to obtain these maps. We begin by summarising the underlying physical principles and theory. Then we describe methods for magnitude  B 1 +   mapping such as actual flip-angle imaging (AFI), saturation-prepared  B 1 +   mapping (e.g., satTFL) and dual refocusing echo acquisition mode (DREAM) that are the basis of widely-applied per-channel complex  B 1 +   mapping methods, as well as methods of pedagogical and/or historical relevance. Next, we describe how relative  B 1 +   mapping with low-flip angle gradient-recalled echo (GRE) scans can determine the relative phases (and relative magnitudes) of  B 1 +   for each channel. We recap the important interferometric approach that is now widely used. We explain how magnitude and phase maps are combined into complex per-channel  B 1 +   maps. We discuss remaining arbitrary factors such as the position-dependent transmit reference phase. We discuss recent practical implementations such as Sandwich TFL, 3DREAM, compressed-sensing SA2RAGE and respiratory-resolved  B 1 +   mapping. We explore the workflow improvements that could accrue if per-channel  B 1 +   maps do not need to be acquired for every subject. This includes deep-learning-based approaches to synthesize  B 1 +   maps from the normal localiser scans, the universal pulses (UPs) approach to precalibrate pulses and variants such as standardised universal pulses (SUPs), Fast-Online Customised (FOCUS) and machine-learning online customisation. We hope to encourage greater openness and harmonisation of these critical calibration steps for parallel transmit pulse design. This will become increasingly important as 7-T pTx MRI is adopted for multisite cross-vendor clinical research studies and to deliver the full scientific potential of new extremely high field human MRIs.

articles.title: Letter to the Editor: Technical feasibility does not establish clinical safety-caution before expanding SpineJack indications in thin pedicles.
Reply to the Letter to the Editor: Hospital-finance implications of AI-assisted mammography.
Multimodality imaging of hepatic cystic echinococcosis: diagnostic approach, differential diagnosis, complications, and post-treatment assessment.
articles.abstract: Cystic echinococcosis (CE), caused by the metacestode of Echinococcus granulosus sensu lato, is a zoonosis that remains endemic across the Middle East, the Mediterranean basin, North Africa and South America, and the liver is the organ most frequently involved. Because serological assays are of limited sensitivity and specificity, imaging carries the diagnostic burden: ultrasonography (US) is the cornerstone for initial diagnosis, staging, treatment planning and longitudinal follow-up; computed tomography (CT) best defines anatomical location, vascular relationships, mural calcification and acute complications such as rupture and superinfection; and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) more faithfully reproduces US-defined staging morphology than CT and provides superior soft-tissue contrast for assessing biliary involvement and separating CE cysts from cystic neoplasms. The aim of this pictorial review is fourfold: to illustrate the US, CT and MRI appearance of each World Health Organization Informal Working Group on Echinococcosis (WHO-IWGE) stage of hepatic CE and to explain how stage assignment translates directly into a stage-specific treatment decision-anti-parasitic treatment, percutaneous treatment, surgery or watch-and-wait; to present, stage by stage, the hepatic lesions that mimic CE and the findings that discriminate them; to depict the wall signs of the CE cyst that become visible with high-frequency linear transducers, including the three-layered wall, adherent brood capsules and hydatid sand; and to review the imaging of complicated CE together with the expected post-treatment appearance, procedure-related complications and the imaging strategy for detecting recurrence.

articles.title: Synovial plica syndromes: a comprehensive overview from embryology to pathology.
articles.abstract: Synovial plicae are folds of synovial tissue in the knee, hip, elbow, and shoulder, representing embryonic remnants of synovial septa. They are usually asymptomatic, but trauma, repetitive microtrauma, or prior surgery can render them thickened and fibrotic, producing pain and mechanical symptoms collectively termed plica syndrome. It is easily overlooked or misdiagnosed because the symptoms are nonspecific and other intra-articular disorders often coexist. This review addresses the embryology, histology, anatomy, clinical presentation, imaging, and treatment of synovial plicae across these joints, with emphasis on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features. MRI is the preferred imaging modality for evaluating suspected plica syndrome, characterizing the fold and associated abnormalities, and excluding alternative causes of joint pain. Pathologic plicae appear thickened and irregular, with increased signal intensity and frequently associated focal synovitis or adjacent chondral damage. Plica thickness alone has limited diagnostic value, as measurements overlap between symptomatic and asymptomatic individuals. Establishing a diagnosis of symptomatic plica syndrome requires correlation of the imaging findings with the clinical presentation. When joint effusion is absent, magnetic resonance (MR) or computed tomography (CT) arthrography improves delineation of the synovial folds and associated lesions. Plica syndrome occurs most often in young, physically active patients, and management is initially conservative. When symptoms are refractory, arthroscopic resection relieves symptoms, particularly when the plica is the only abnormality and the cartilage is preserved. Most outcome data derive from the knee and the elbow.

articles.title: Performance of Deep Learning Algorithms for Segmentation of Shoulder Anatomy on MRI: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: To synthesize the performance and methodological characteristics of fully automated deep learning algorithms for shoulder magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) segmentation. This systematic review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. CENTRAL, PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore were searched from inception through July 17, 2026. The protocol specified fully automated deep learning-based pixel-wise segmentation of shoulder MRI, an expert-derived MRI-space reference standard, and quantitative segmentation metrics. Two reviewers independently screened records; unresolved disagreements were adjudicated by a senior reviewer. Overlapping datasets were linked during synthesis. Of 354 identified records, 169 duplicates were removed, 185 records were screened, and 53 full-text reports were assessed. Thirty-five reports were included (31 journal articles and 4 full conference papers; 2018-2026). U-Net-based encoder-decoder architectures predominated, with additional region-based, transformer, adversarial, and autoencoder approaches. Dice similarity coefficients ranged from approximately 0.81-0.99 for osseous targets, 0.71-0.99 for shoulder muscles, and 0.58-0.94 for tendon or tear regions; intersection-over-union values for tear or surgical-planning regions ranged from 0.45-0.83. MRI protocols and validation designs were heterogeneous, and most reports described retrospective single-center investigations. Five reports used independent external test sets; several others included multicenter images. Overlapping cohorts precluded a valid pooled participant count. Deep learning achieved high accuracy for shoulder bones and rotator-cuff muscles in selected datasets, whereas tear-region performance was more variable. Multicenter patient-level validation and standardized annotation and reporting are needed before routine clinical deployment.

articles.title: Percutaneous and endovascular procedures in adrenal disease: indications, technique, and outcomes.
articles.abstract: Adrenal masses are found on roughly 4-5% of abdominal imaging studies, and the proportion rises with age. Most are benign, non-functioning adenomas that need imaging characterization and hormonal screening but no intervention. The remainder, comprising metastases, adrenocortical carcinoma, pheochromocytoma and hormonally active adenomas, raise questions that computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging cannot always settle; in these cases image-guided procedures can help. Percutaneous biopsy is reserved for hormonally inactive lesions whose benignity imaging has not established and whose histology would change management. Adrenal venous sampling remains the reference method for lateralizing aldosterone excess in primary aldosteronism and therefore decides who is offered adrenalectomy, although success depends heavily on operator experience and local protocol. Thermal ablation has produced biochemical and blood-pressure responses in selected aldosterone-producing adenomas and local control of limited metastases, but the evidence is largely nonrandomized and does not establish equivalence with surgery. Transarterial embolization serves three purposes: hemostasis in adrenal hemorrhage, devascularization before resection of hypervascular tumors, and functional treatment of aldosteronism, now supported by one small randomized trial. Each procedure carries hazards peculiar to the gland (catecholamine crisis, adrenal insufficiency after bilateral treatment, non-target embolization) that shape patient selection and periprocedural monitoring. This review covers indications, technique, outcomes and complications for each. Surgery remains the treatment of choice for most operable patients. Interventional radiology is most useful when the indications for sampling, ablation or embolization are recognized early and discussed at the multidisciplinary meeting, not only after surgery has been declined.

Multiparametric quantitative MRI in knee osteoarthritis: evidence and requirements for interpretation and reporting.
articles.abstract: Quantitative MRI can characterize cartilage and other joint tissues beyond visible structural damage, but its contribution to individual management of knee osteoarthritis remains uncertain. This narrative review examines the evidence needed to interpret quantitative measurements, combine parameters, and report their uncertainty. An initial PubMed search in June 2026 was supplemented on 14 September 2026 by an updated PubMed search and broader Embase and Web of Science searches. Targeted full-text assessment addressed incremental value, outcome timing, validation, and measurement error. Selected development studies found better discrimination with integrated diffusion and relaxation measurements than with individual parameters, whereas other combined imaging models did not improve on simpler comparators. Longitudinal associations were outcome-specific, and independent external validation was limited. Treatment studies showed inconsistent agreement between imaging changes and symptomatic benefit. We propose a five-step interpretation framework that establishes the clinical question, verifies technical adequacy, assesses morphology and comparable reference data, evaluates measurement uncertainty, and separates observations from clinical inferences. Two hypothetical scenarios illustrate its application. Quantitative MRI currently provides its strongest support as a controlled research measurement. Demonstrated reproducibility, an appropriate comparator, and evidence of added decision value are required before a quantitative finding can justify patient-level diagnostic, prognostic, or treatment-response claims.

articles.title: An anatomy-aware spatio-temporal generative extrapolation network for distal ascending aorta restoration in standard echocardiographic views.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: In two-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography (TTE), the standard parasternal long-axis (PLAX) view enables reliable evaluation of the aortic valve and aortic root. Owing to the limited field of view of the ultrasound probe and rib-window occlusion, the distal ascending aorta (AA) is frequently truncated, compromising the diagnosis of aortic aneurysm and dilation. PURPOSE: We aim to address the incomplete visualization of the distal AA in standard PLAX views. By aggregating fragmented anatomical features intermittently visible in adjacent frames, we enhance the clarity of vessel wall edges and generate the distal AA structure, thereby completing the missing AA imagery in standard PLAX views. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively collected 1160 TTE videos from Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital (August 2022 - December 2024), all showing complete AA anatomy. After de-identification, 1059 cases were randomly split into training/validation/test sets (6:2:2), and 101 cases were reserved for observer agreement experiments. An additional 152 videos from three different device models (EPIQ CVX, GE Voluson E10, Resona A20T) formed an external validation set. Two training data types were constructed: (i) dual-view synchronous data - a standard PLAX sequence and an AO-PLAX sequence acquired after a cranial probe shift, phase-matched at end diastole (ED); and (ii) locally masked data - the distal AA region was masked, forcing the model to infer missing anatomy from left-side context. Input sequences of five frames (ED ± 2) were extracted. The proposed Spatio-Temporal Ascending-Aorta generative adversarial network (STAA-GAN) first aligns adjacent frames using an Edge Boosted Feature Alignment (EBFA) module with multi-stage modulated deformable convolutions. A channel-wise fusion strategy then aggregates temporally aligned features. The fused representation is fed into a Swin-UNet generator enhanced with a Strip based Cross window Prediction (SCP) module to capture long-range structural dependencies. Training employs a composite loss including pixel reconstruction, feature reconstruction, texture consistency, relativistic average least-squares GAN (RaLSGAN), temporal coherence, and structure-aware terms, with data-dependent weighting. Statistical analyzes included Bland-Altman, Passing-Bablok regression, paired t-tests with Cohen's d, Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons, and two one-sided tests (TOST, Δ = 0.2  cm  ). RESULTS: STAA-GAN achieved the best image-quality values among the compared methods, with peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) = 22.51 dB, structural similarity index (SSIM) = 0.7574, multi-scale structural similarity index (MS-SSIM) = 0.8598, and learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS) = 0.1758. All 12 pairwise comparisons (SRN, IOH, and U-Transformer versus STAA-GAN, designated as the reference group) remained statistically significant after Bonferroni correction (  α 1 = 0.00417  ), with absolute effect sizes ranging from 0.255 to 3.439. The per-frame inference time was 203 ms. In clinical consistency validation, the mean difference between measurements on generated and original images was ≤ 0.01   cm with 95% limits of agreement within ± 0.13   cm; TOST with Δ = 0.2   cm confirmed clinical equivalence for all comparisons ( p < 0.001  ). The segmentation Dice coefficient on generated images averaged 0.913 ± 0.045  across five cross-validation folds. External validation on three different ultrasound devices (Philips, GE, Mindray) maintained consistent equivalence (TOST p < 0.001  , Cohen's d < 0.2  ). These results demonstrate that STAA-GAN produces clinically interchangeable distal ascending aorta images with high fidelity and real-time feasibility. CONCLUSIONS: STAA-GAN enables extrapolation of the missing distal ascending aorta in standard PLAX views, achieving improved image quality and clinically equivalent diameter measurements on both internal and external validation datasets. These findings support its potential for assisting distal ascending aorta assessment in routine echocardiography.

articles.title: A public projection imaging dataset for fieldfree line magnetic particle imaging.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Magnetic particle imaging (MPI) is an emerging biomedical imaging modality. In recent years, human-scale MPI systems based on field-free line MPI (FFL-MPI) projection imaging have been increasingly advanced. However, the lack of publicly available FFL-MPI datasets has hindered algorithm development and system performance optimization. To address this issue, this paper presents a dataset based on the FFL-MPI system, named FFL-MPI-Data, through simulation studies and data acquisition from a real-world system. ACQUISITION AND VALIDATION METHODS: The FFL-MPI-Data contains both simulated and measured data spanning multiple domains and harmonics. The measured dataset was acquired using a self-developed scanner, which collected raw voltage signals, sinograms, and reconstructed images from 100 physical phantoms. The simulated dataset was generated via a custom-built simulation framework that replicates the key parameters of the experimental scanner, with the MNIST dataset employed as digital phantoms. The simulation framework is validated by evaluating the characteristics of harmonic images output from numerical phantoms. Furthermore, the utility and reliability of the dataset were verified by evaluating the performance of a deep learning model (FBPConvNet) on both sparse-angle and limited-angle reconstruction tasks. DATA FORMAT AND USAGE NOTES: The FFL-MPI-Data repository adopts the Hierarchical Data Format (HDF5) for data storage, which contains both phantom data and associated metadata. The dataset is publicly available on the Zenodo platform. Furthermore, we provide open-source codes for data processing, image reconstruction, simulation implementation, and deep learning demonstrations at https://github.com/BUAALGH/FFL-MPI-Data. Users can readily access and utilize the FFL-MPI-Data dataset via the provided example code. POTENTIAL APPLICATIONS: FFL-MPI-Data represents a publicly accessible dataset for FFL-MPI, addressing the scarcity of available data for projection imaging research in this domain. This dataset is expected to facilitate the development and validation of image reconstruction algorithms, including investigations into signal processing, multi-domain reconstruction, and multi-harmonic reconstruction for specific tasks such as sparse-angle and limited-angle reconstruction.

articles.title: Robustness of proliferation-based constrained spatiotemporal fractionation under setup and radiobiological uncertainties in liver radiotherapy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Spatiotemporal fractionation redistributes dose between fractions and may reduce normal-tissue exposure. Its sensitivity to setup uncertainty and radiobiological assumptions requires evaluation before clinical use. PURPOSE: To evaluate proliferation-based constrained spatiotemporal fractionation (p-cSTF) under geometric and radiobiological perturbations in conventionally fractionated liver radiotherapy. The focus was normal-liver dose. METHODS: Thirty-five patients with hepatocellular carcinoma were included. Uniform fractionation, proliferation-based spatiotemporal fractionation (p-STF), and p-cSTF were evaluated over 25 fractions. The primary comparison matched nominal mean gross tumor volume (GTV) biologically effective dose (BED); a supplementary comparison matched nominal model-derived tumor control probability (TCP). Setup tests comprised 18 single-axis offsets (± 1, ± 2, and ± 3 mm) and 24 transverse voxel offsets, each held constant over treatment. Thirty scenarios varied biological-model parameters; precision checks used two 480-scenario sequences. Nominal dose grids were evaluated under perturbations without reoptimization. Endpoints included physical dose, BED, equivalent dose in 2 Gy fractions (EQD2), coverage, and response-model scores. RESULTS: Under biological-parameter variation, normal-liver (liver excluding GTV) BED was 26.22 ± 7.00 Gy for p-cSTF, 28.18 ± 7.57 Gy for Uniform, and 28.05 ± 7.76 Gy for p-STF. Corresponding EQD2 values were 14.92 ± 3.96, 16.05 ± 4.29, and 15.96 ± 4.39 Gy. Values are cohort means and between-patient standard deviations of patient-specific scenario means. Normal-liver BED remained lower with p-cSTF after nominal TCP matching, although fixed transverse offsets produced lower GTV TCP than with Uniform. Expanded sampling retained the direction of the liver-dose difference; the original 30 scenarios did not meet the specified precision criteria for scenario variability. CONCLUSIONS: P-cSTF retained a simulated normal-liver dose advantage under the tested perturbations, including after nominal TCP matching. This advantage must be considered alongside target-response trade-offs and uncertainty in scenario-variability estimates. Clinical toxicity and treatment deliverability were not evaluated.

articles.title: Diffusion Prior-Driven Vision-Language Adaptation for Few-Shot Medical Anomaly Detection.
articles.abstract: Unsupervised medical anomaly detection faces dual challenges of pathological data scarcity and domain gaps when transferring general-purpose vision-language models to fine-grained tasks. This study aims to address the misalignment between global semantic representations and local pathological nuances by proposing a novel hybrid supervision framework. We propose a flexible vision-language adaptation framework in which diffusion-based pseudo-anomaly synthesis serves as an optional training enhancement. For CheXpert and BUSI, region-guided diffusion generates localized pseudo-anomalies to provide additional discriminative supervision. For BrainMRI, the framework is trained exclusively on normal reference images without any synthetic anomaly augmentation, allowing us to assess its effectiveness independently of the diffusion synthesis component. The architecture incorporates a local-enhanced feature rectifier to enhance local textural representation, a zero-initialized hypersphere-aligned residual adapter for stable cross-modal manifold alignment, and a temperature-scaled mapmaker for multi-scale dense anomaly localization. Performance was evaluated across three medical imaging modalities under multiple few-shot configurations. Our method remains highly competitive compared to state-of-the-art approaches in terms of image-level detection and pixel-level localization. On the ultrasound dataset under a 32-shot setting, the framework achieved an image-level area under the curve of 94.2% and a pixel-level area under the curve of 96.6%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework across the evaluated medical imaging modalities under different training configurations. In particular, its competitive performance on BrainMRI without synthetic anomaly augmentation suggests that the vision-language adaptation framework can remain effective when offline pseudo-anomaly generation is unavailable. The code involved in this study is publicly available on website https://github.com/SWLee777/DiffVLA .

articles.title: Propagation of Low-Dose-Induced Noise Characteristics Across Deep Learning Layers in CT Imaging.
articles.abstract: Dose reduction in computed tomography (CT) imaging impacts diagnostic accuracy for human observers and potentially artificial intelligence (AI) systems. As noise propagates through an AI model, its characteristics change, possibly influencing model performance. This study aims to develop a configurable low-dose CT simulation tool in image-space and analyze noise behavior in deep learning (DL) layers. The noise characteristics were quantified using the noise power spectrum (NPS) within homogeneous phantom regions. NPS area under the curve (intensity) and median frequency (texture) were reported. Low-dose CT images were simulated using a custom program that was calibrated for configurable noise intensity and texture. Noise was generated at texture levels. Pre-trained U-Net features were extracted from reference and simulated low-dose images, enabling NPS-based analysis of noise propagation across deep learning layers. NPS from simulated low-dose CT images matched reference NPS for various intensity and texture values. Feature analysis revealed progressive convergence of noise characteristics across deep learning layers, with batch normalization mitigating amplification observed after convolution and ReLU activation. Differences in noise texture between low-dose simulations converge along the U-Net contracting path. The image-space simulation tool offers a viable alternative for researchers lacking access to raw data, supporting future AI-focused dose optimization studies. However, whether these outcomes translate to segmentation performance remains unclear and warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Data Leakage and Unverified Provenance in Public Brain Tumor MRI Datasets: A Systematic Audit.
articles.abstract: Brain tumor MRI classification studies routinely report accuracies above 99%, yet many public datasets in this domain trace to a few original sources and are often combined or cross-validated without accounting for shared origin. We audited seven brain tumor MRI datasets (34,525 images) for leakage within datasets and overlap between datasets typically treated as independent. Internal leakage was detected with perceptual hashing and rotation-aware structural similarity. Cross-dataset overlap was detected with ResNet-50 embedding similarity, checked against a random-pair baseline, a DenseNet-121 sensitivity analysis, and blinded two-rater review (all 75 sampled above-threshold pairs were true duplicates; 95% CI 95.1-100). A further blinded review just below the threshold found roughly half of the sampled pairs were also duplicates, so reported overlap is a lower bound. True-duplicate leakage between training and evaluation splits occurred in three of four datasets with predefined splits, including a peer-reviewed dataset and one documented as overlap-free. For 14 of 16 dataset pairs, 15.6-99.1% of the smaller dataset's images were automatically matched to the other, including datasets described as collected from named hospitals. In a controlled experiment on the one dataset with patient identifiers, image-level splitting yielded higher accuracy than patient-level splitting (97.10 ± 0.69% vs. 91.82 ± 2.77%; Welch's t-test, p = 0.017), with a 10.1-point drop in meningioma F1. This addresses within-dataset correlation only, so it is a conservative estimate of total inflation. Reported performance warrants cautious interpretation, and tooling for verifying dataset independence is lacking. We propose a checklist for dataset creators and researchers.

articles.title: From a Clinical Mammography Archive to an AI-Ready Imaging Cohort: A Single-Center Implementation and Evidence Audit.
articles.abstract: Clinical imaging archives contain potentially valuable research data, but records retained for patient care do not automatically form an analysis-ready cohort. In this single-center study, we implemented and audited a metadata-driven workflow that separated patient-day indexing, image/report availability, study-defined bilateral four-view structure, quality control state, and pathology linkage. Among 13,203 indexed patient-day groups from January 2015 through December 2020, 5390 were DICOM-bearing, and 3169 of these met the metadata-defined bilateral four-view requirement (58.8%). The same requirement was met by 3168 of 5381 DICOM- and report-matched folders (58.9%), whereas 7813 report-linked groups lacked retained DICOM and were not assessable for image structure. Pathology was examined independently rather than as a nested endpoint; the strict-window diagnostic biopsy analysis identified 229 strict-window high-confidence groups. Thus, archive size, joint image/report availability, structural eligibility, and outcome evidence defined different analytical states. This implementation shows how established imaging-informatics principles can make cohort construction auditable within one institution; transferability requires independent external implementation and evaluation.

articles.title: The Deep Learning-Based Prediction Method for Cervical Lymph Node Metastasis of Thyroid Cancer Based on Multimodal Data.
articles.abstract: Thyroid cancer is a common malignant tumor worldwide, and there is a risk of misdiagnosis or over-treatment for small-sized thyroid cancer. The key to eliminating this risk lies in predicting cervical lymph node metastasis. The traditional manual prediction methods are not ideal, so this paper proposes an intelligent prediction method based on deep learning. This method is based on common clinical examination data, including ultrasound images, ultrasound image text descriptions, and blood test data. A deep convolutional neural network model is proposed using data from these three modalities as inputs. The model integrates multimodal data features through mean cross-attention and extracts fine-grained classification information from the fused feature map through a bilinear CNN network, demonstrating strong feature discrimination ability. Through collecting data and conducting various experiments, the experimental results show that the model proposed in this paper has good performance in predicting cervical lymph node metastasis, is better than the manual prediction, and has broad application prospects. Future research will continue to strive for data collection, increasing the amount of collected data and improving multi-center representativeness, and enhancing the diagnostic and predictive capabilities of the network model through technological improvements.

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance of Magnetic Resonance Elastography Versus Vibration-Controlled Transient Elastography for Liver Fibrosis Staging in Steatotic Liver Disease.
articles.abstract: Gravitational magnetic resonance elastography (GT-MRE) enables comprehensive biomechanical liver characterization and may overcome limitations of conventional elastography techniques. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of two- and three-dimensional (2D and 3D) GT-MRE compared with 2D acoustic MRE (AC-MRE) and vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) for liver fibrosis staging. In this prospective study, patients with suspected or known steatotic liver disease underwent GT-MRE (2D and 3D, gradient-echo sequences) and AC-MRE (2D, spin-echo echo-planar imaging) at 1.5 T, plus VCTE with a median interval to MRE of 37 days (IQR, 20-124 days; range, 0-372 days). Statistical analyses included generalized additive models, ordinal logistic regression, and decision tree-based classification. Diagnostic performance was assessed using cumulative receiver operating characteristic analysis and corresponding areas under the curve (AUCs). Ninety-one participants (median age, 55 years [IQR, 45-64]; 41 women) were included, of whom 35 (38%) had histopathological correlation. In the biopsy-confirmed subgroup, 3D GT-MRE-derived viscoelastic parameters showed promising exploratory performance for early fibrosis classification. Wave attenuation achieved AUCs of 0.91 for F0 versus ≥ F1 and 0.99 for ≤ F1 versus ≥ F2, while phase angle yielded an AUC of 0.88 for F0 versus ≥ F1, with numerically higher AUCs than conventional stiffness-based metrics. For advanced fibrosis thresholds, all modalities performed well (AUC ≥ 0.84). Obuchowski measures for 3D-derived parameters were 0.95-0.96. Internally cross-validated multiparametric modeling achieved an accuracy of up to 92%. VCTE measurements plateaued beyond F3, whereas AC- and GT-MRE metrics continued to increase with fibrosis severity. 3D GT-MRE-derived viscoelastic parameters showed promising performance for liver fibrosis classification and provided biomechanical information complementary to conventional stiffness measurements. Given the limited biopsy-confirmed sample and marked class imbalance at F0, these findings require validation in larger independent cohorts before clinical implementation.

articles.title: NA-DIP: A Noise-Aware Deep Image Prior for Generating Dedicated Brain PET-Quality Images from Whole-Body PET Acquisitions.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To generate dedicated brain PET-quality images from routine whole-body PET acquisitions by robustly enhancing the brain region using a noise-aware deep image prior (NA-DIP) approach. METHODS: NA-DIP integrates anatomy-guided priors derived from patient-specific μ-maps or MR images, a regularization strategy for enhanced denoising, and a variance-based early stopping criterion that adaptively monitors noise without requiring prior noise assumptions. Using noisy PET images as self-supervised targets, the method was first evaluated using simulation data spanning three noise levels to investigate the trade-off between noise suppression and bias. It was then applied to brain images extracted from 90-s-per-bed-position whole-body acquisitions from 15 pediatric FDG-PET studies spanning a broad range of patient demographics, physiological variability, and image noise levels. Using the corresponding 360-s-per-bed-position dedicated brain scans as the reference, NA-DIP-enhanced images were evaluated for noise reduction, standardized uptake value (SUV) accuracy, and image quality in a blinded reader study. RESULTS: NA-DIP demonstrated a superior noise-bias trade-off compared with Gaussian filtering and conventional DIP stopping strategies, particularly under high-noise conditions. The inclusion of MR or μ-map guidance further improved performance. Across pediatric patients, NA-DIP-enhanced 90-s images exhibited lower noise than the corresponding 360-s dedicated brain images while showing modest variability in SUV measurements. Blinded readers rated the NA-DIP-enhanced images as comparable to or better than dedicated brain images in most cases. CONCLUSION: NA-DIP enhanced brain PET images from whole-body acquisitions demonstrated good quantitative agreement and image quality comparable to or exceeding the reference, supporting the feasibility of eliminating separate dedicated brain scans.

articles.title: Training Interbrain Synchrony through Dyadic Neurofeedback Modulates Empathy-for-Pain.
articles.abstract: Dyadic neurofeedback offers a socially grounded approach for modulating neural processes that unfold between interacting individuals. While recent work demonstrates that dyadic neurofeedback can enhance inter-brain synchrony during interaction, whether its effects extend beyond the trained dyad remains unclear. Here, we examined whether dyadic neurofeedback targeting inter-brain synchrony in the inferior frontal gyrus (IFG) is associated with changes in empathy-for-pain toward unfamiliar social targets. One hundred and eighty-six participants, randomly assigned to dyads, completed three neurofeedback training sessions within one week. Feedback was contingent on real-time IFG inter-brain synchrony in the neurofeedback group or on prerecorded signals in the sham-feedback control group. Empathy-for-pain was assessed before and after training. IFG inter-brain synchrony increased significantly across sessions in the neurofeedback group but not in the control group. Empathy-for-pain ratings showed different trajectories across conditions in the primary raw-data analysis, decreasing significantly in the sham-feedback group while remaining relatively stable in the neurofeedback group. A secondary analysis adjusting for a previously observed task-specific test-retest decline showed a significant increase in the neurofeedback group. Individuals with lower baseline trait empathy showed larger training-related increases in IFG inter-brain synchrony. Network analyses suggested broader changes involving IFG-IPL connectivity. Structural equation modeling further identified significant associations among training-related intra-brain synchrony, inter-brain synchrony, and empathy-for-pain change, consistent with the proposed relationship among these processes. Together, the findings indicate that dyadic neurofeedback can modulate IFG inter-brain synchrony across repeated training and may influence the trajectory of empathy-for-pain responding beyond the immediate training partner.

articles.title: Desync and connect: Noninvasive MEG evidence of long-range coupling between locally desynchronized regions.
articles.abstract: A prevailing assumption in systems neuroscience is that long-range phase coupling between cortical regions requires locally synchronized oscillatory activity within each interacting area. Here we ask whether distal phase coupling can be detected from MEG data when both interacting regions undergo concurrent event-related desynchronization (ERD). Using controlled simulations with progressively disrupted local phase coherence, we first establish that the Context-Dependent PSIICOS (CD-PSIICOS) framework - a projection-based connectivity estimator that separates power-dominated spatial leakage from interaction-specific cross-spectral structure - can recover distal coupling under increasing local phase dispersion, whereas estimators based on the imaginary part of the cross-spectrum fail at near-zero lags. We then analyzed recordings of a center-out reaching dataset from nine participants. A group decomposition of the coupling time courses identifies four long-range networks in alpha (8-13 Hz) and two in beta (15-25 Hz), each with its own time window. For each network we follow the local connections between its own sources as the power-dominated subspace is projected out, separating leakage-driven from leakage-resistant local coupling. In the earliest alpha network the leakage-resistant pairs stay at or below their pre-stimulus level at every rank while the power of the same sources falls, so this interhemispheric interaction may have no stable local counterpart. In the beta networks such a counterpart does survive, but the coupling it carries is an order of magnitude weaker than the long-range coupling of the same sources. Only in the latest alpha window, by which time power has returned to baseline, do local and long-range coupling rise together. Factorising the coupling into the amplitude of the single-trial cross-terms and the consistency of their phases separates the same cases: in the networks without a local counterpart, phase consistency increases inside the window while the amplitude of the cross-terms declines, whereas in the network whose local coupling rises with it, the increase reflects a growth of the cross-terms themselves rather than any improvement in their phase agreement. Long-range phase coupling can therefore persist, and in places strengthen, between regions undergoing macroscopic ERD, and noninvasive MEG can resolve this dissociation when leakage-aware estimation is employed.

articles.title: Early identification of the risk of foot ulcers in patients with diabetes based on CT multi-radiomics nomogram.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop CT-based multi-radiomic signatures for the early identification of diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) risk. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 190 patients with diabetes who underwent lower-extremity CT angiography (CTA) were retrospectively included.
