Lower-limb vessels were segmented using the general CT image segmentation (gCIS) model, and radiomic features were extracted from axial lower-limb CTA images. Minimum redundancy maximum relevance (mRMR) and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression were applied for feature selection, and a Rad-score was computed to build a radiomics model. A radiomics nomogram integrating the Rad-score with clinical characteristics was constructed using multivariate logistic regression. Model value was evaluated with receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis. RESULTS: Twelve radiomic features were retained after selection. The radiomics nomogram, which combined clinical factors with the Rad-score, achieved area-under-the-curve (AUC) values of 0.971 (95% CI: 0.946-0.997) in the training set and 0.887 (95% CI:0.842-0.932) in the testing set, exceeding those of the standalone radiomics model (training: 0.875, 95% CI 0.819-0.931; testing: 0.854, 95% CI 0.731-0.977). ROC and decision curve analyses indicated that the radiomics nomogram had greater reliability than the standalone radiomics model. CONCLUSION: In summary, the lower-limb arterial vessel-based radiomics nomogram facilitates early DFU risk identification, offering a precise, objective, and easily interpretable method for predicting DFU at an early stage.

articles.title: Beam-width-corrected DOI resolution measurement of dual-ended readout PET detectors.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Dual-ended readout PET detectors provide depth-of-interaction (DOI) information for reducing parallax errors in high-resolution PET imaging. This study compared LYSO detectors with different inter-crystal reflectors and investigated the effect of irradiation beam width on DOI resolution measurements under electronic collimation. APPROACH: Two 28 × 28 LYSO arrays with 0.75 × 0.75 × 10 mm³ crystals and BaSO₄ or E60 reflectors were characterized in terms of flood-map quality, energy resolution, and DOI resolution. Part of E60 detector (8×8 crystals) was further measured using three irradiation geometries with beam widths of 0.80 mm, 0.62 mm, and 0.46 mm. A beam-width correction was applied to the measured DOI resolution, and the effects of energy selection and empirical flood-map-based inter-crystal scattering (ICS) filtering were evaluated. MAIN RESULTS: The BaSO₄ detector showed better flood-map quality and energy resolution, whereas the E60 detector showed better DOI resolution. In the 400-650 keV energy window, the measured average DOI resolutions of entire 28 × 28 LYSO pixels with irradiation beam width of 1.00 mm were 1.92 and 1.75 mm for the BaSO₄ and E60 detectors, respectively. For the selected 8 × 8 crystal region of the E60 detector, the corrected DOI resolution by subtracting the irradiation beam width improved from 1.19 mm for all events to 1.01 mm after energy selection, and further to 0.86 mm after additional empirical flood-map-based ICS filtering. SIGNIFICANCE: Irradiation beam width introduces a geometry-dependent contribution to DOI resolution measurements. Beam-width correction enables more consistent DOI characterization under different irradiation geometries.

articles.title: Volumetric Chest CT Report Generation via State-Space Visual Prompting and Clinical-Fact Alignment.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To address the memory bottlenecks of 3D sequence modeling and the factual hallucinations associated with cross-entropy optimization in automated 3D chest CT report generation. APPROACH: We propose an end-to-end framework that couples perception refinement with clinical-fact alignment. First, a hybrid perception module integrates spatial visual encoding with a bidirectional state-space model to capture global anatomical topology at linear computational complexity. Second, a lesion-aware visual prompting module extracts key pathological signals through cross-view synergy and adaptive residual gating. Finally, the text decoder is fine-tuned with the Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) algorithm under an asymmetric composite reward, reducing its reliance on normal templates. MAIN RESULTS: Experiments on the CTRG-Chest-548K dataset show that the proposed method achieves competitive natural language generation performance and, more importantly, a substantial improvement in clinical accuracy. The RadGraph F1 score increases from 41.89 to 44.63 relative to the strongest baseline, indicating reduced factual hallucination. SIGNIFICANCE: Combined with a 71% reduction in peak inference memory, these results indicate that the framework is a practical step toward deployable and clinically reliable automated CT interpretation.

articles.title: Image reconstruction based on FWHM-Energy Joint Weighting for Magnetic Particle Imaging.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Magnetic particle imaging (MPI) enables high-sensitivity quantitative imaging by detecting the nonlinear magnetization response of superparamagnetic nanoparticles. FFPgridded MPI has been developed to reduce system complexity, and its multi-harmonic extension exploits harmonic-dependent information to balance spatial resolution and SNR. However, an appropriate weighting strategy is required to utilize complementary information across harmonics. We propose an image reconstruction method based on full width at half maximum (FWHM)-energy joint weighting, which combines PSF-derived FWHM with either L2-norm harmonic energy or noise energy to achieve a favorable trade-off between spatial resolution enhancement and reconstruction stability. APPROACH: In the FFP-gridded multi-harmonic fusion framework, the 3 rd , 5 th , 7 th , and 9 th harmonic components are jointly used for image reconstruction. Since different harmonics exhibit distinct characteristics in signal intensity, noise level, and spatial resolution, optimizing their weights is essential for improving reconstruction quality. Traditional weighting strategies based on amplitude, signal energy, and noise characteristics were implemented as comparison methods. On this basis, two FWHM-energy joint weighting strategies were developed: L2norm energy-FWHM weighting for balancing resolution improvement and artifact suppression, and noise-energy-FWHM weighting for enhancing the spatial resolution of noise-suppressed reconstruction. MAIN RESULTS: The proposed methods were validated through numerical simulations and phantom experiments under different noise conditions and phantoms. The results demonstrate that the FWHM-energy joint weighting strategies improved reconstruction quality compared with traditional weighting methods. By incorporating spatial resolution information into harmonic weighting, the proposed methods achieved a more favorable balance among spatial resolution, artifact suppression, and reconstruction stability. SIGNIFICANCE: The proposed method introduces FWHM-energy joint weighting strategies for multi-harmonic MPI reconstruction, enabling spatial resolution enhancement while preserving reconstruction stability. Future work will focus on extending this framework to adaptive weighting schemes and more complex scenarios, thereby improving the applicability of multiharmonic MPI reconstruction.

articles.title: Reverberant magnetic resonance elastography and NODDI provide complementary characterisation of age-related brain changes in healthy adults.
articles.abstract: Age-related changes in brain microstructure and mechanical properties are essential for understanding neurodegeneration and improving early diagnosis. We asked whether tissue microstructure explains the age-related decline in brain stiffness. To test this, we related stiffness measured using reverberant magnetic resonance elastography (MRE) to tissue microstructure, assessed by neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging (NODDI).Approach. Twenty-eight healthy volunteers (22 to 76 years) underwent 50 Hz MRE at 3T. NODDI parameters (the isotropic volume fraction, Fiso; orientation dispersion index, ODI; neurite density index, NDI) were computed from diffusion-weighted images in 26 subjects. We analyzed global gray and white matter, as well as 13 deep brain regions. Age associations were evaluated using Spearman correlations. Multivariate regression was used to test whether NODDI parameters predicted shear modulus independently of age. All tests used Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction.Main results. Shear modulus decreased with age in both gray matter (ρ= -0.62, p = 0.0005) and white matter (ρ= -0.60, p = 0.0007), and in nine of 13 deep brain regions after FDR correction. Fiso (ρ = +0.55, p = 0.004) and NDI (ρ= +0.45, p = 0.023) increased with age in gray matter; no NODDI parameter changed significantly with age in white matter. Across the six global multivariate tests (gray and white matter times three NODDI parameters), only the gray-matter Fiso independently predicted shear modulus after adjusting for age (β= -3.230, pFDR = 0.010), and no NODDI parameter predicted white matter stiffness. This association did not survive FDR correction after additional adjustment for sex (pFDR = 0.073).Significance. These findings suggest that cortical free water accumulation is the microstructural measure most closely associated with age-related softening in this cohort, pending confirmation in larger, sex-balanced cohorts, and support a multi-modal approach to characterizing age-related brain changes.

articles.title: Instance-Specific Brain Image Registration: Learning Deformable Fields from a Single Image Pair without External Datasets.
articles.abstract: To eliminate the reliance on large-scale external training datasets and achieve high-precision alignment for complex brain structures by overcoming the prevalent challenges of data scarcity and domain shifts in current deep learning-based registration methods.Approach: We propose a novel Instance-Specific Deep Brain Registration Framework that independently trains a dedicated model for each specific image pair. By reconceptualizing a single image pair as an internal dataset generator, we introduce a Multi-Scale Random Patch Learning strategy to construct a diverse local-to-global sample space. Architecturally, we design a Context-Aware Flow Predictor integrated with a Recurrent Context Transfer mechanism within a coarse-to-fine paradigm. Furthermore, a Topology-Aware Adaptive Optimization strategy is incorporated during the inference phase. By dynamically tracking the local spatial folding status, it adaptively adjusts spatial regularization to effectively suppress topological distortions while maximizing voxel-level accuracy.Main results: Extensive experiments on mono-modal, multi-modal, and pathological brain MRI datasets demonstrate that our method can handle large anatomical deformations without relying on external training datasets. It achieves highly competitive registration performance compared to mainstream population-based and implicit neural representation methods. Crucially, it balances this alignment precision with effective numerical topology preservation.Significance: This framework challenges the traditional population-based learning paradigm, offering a highly flexible, robust, and promising solution for practical neuroimage analysis, particularly in clinical scenarios characterized by extreme data scarcity and complex cross-modality variations.

articles.title: BeamGAN: a physics-informed conditional generative adversarial network for Monte-Carlo-free portal dose image prediction from incident fluence maps.
articles.abstract: To develop and validate a Monte-Carlo-free deep learning framework that predicts EPID portal dose images directly from treatment-planning-system (TPS) exported incident fluence maps, enabling real-time patient-specific quality assurance (QA) without Monte Carlo (MC) simulation or empirical per-machine commissioning.Approach. We propose BeamGAN, a physics-informed conditional generative adversarial network. A three-channel input-TPS incident fluence, its Sobel gradient map, and a beam's-eye-view (BEV) target-thickness projection ray-traced through the planning CT with the PTV mask-embeds geometric and edge-scatter priors into an eight-level U-Net generator with a PatchGAN discriminator and an auxiliary registration network. The framework was trained on 91 head-and-neck IMRT patients (split 64/15/12) from one Elekta Versa HD linac, benchmarked against a Brownian-Bridge diffusion baseline (BiBBDM), and evaluated by input-channel ablation and error-injection sensitivity tests.Main results. BeamGAN achieved gamma passing rates (GPR) of 97.40 ± 0.67% (3%/3 mm), 95.42 ± 0.99% (3%/2 mm) and 87.00 ± 1.63% (2%/2 mm; 10% threshold), outperforming BiBBDM (83.32 ± 2.43%, 77.08 ± 3.20% and 67.20 ± 2.45%). On the held-out test set (n = 12), the median GPR was 95.47% (IQR 94.86-96.27) at the TG-218 primary criterion 3%/2 mm; 8/12 cases met the institutional ≥95% acceptance threshold and all 12 exceeded the 90% action level. Ablation identified the fluence-gradient channel as the dominant contributor, with the anatomical prior providing complementary gains. Sensitivity analysis established a criterion-dependent error hierarchy: systematic MLC errors were most detectable (ΔGPR up to 21.23% at 1%/1 mm), followed by collimator rotation (10.31%), whereas MU scaling and setup errors produced marginal effects. BEV computation required 0.3-0.5 s per beam and inference under 50 ms.Significance. Embedded geometric priors can approximate explicit MC scatter modelling in portal dose prediction, removing a principal computational barrier to real-time EPID-based verification within the validated configuraiton. Multi-institutional validation is warranted before clinical deployment.

articles.title: Microwave Dielectric Property Reconstruction of Healthy and Tumor Rat Breast Tissues From In Vivo Measurements Using Generative AI.
articles.abstract: Rapid identification of suspicious breast lesions remains challenging, sincepathological analysis following biopsy requires hours to days, limiting real-timedecision-making, particularly during surgical procedures. Open-ended coaxial probe(OECP)-based methods have shown promise for characterizing target tissues throughestimation of dielectric properties (DPs) from the measured reflection coefficient (S11).Conventional DP calculation from OECP measurements S11 is commonly performed usingiterative methods, while recent studies have also explored artificial intelligence (AI)-basedapproaches for DP estimation. In these studies, AI models were developed using eithersynthetic datasets or limited ex vivo measurement data. In contrast, this study presents agenerative AI approach for direct estimation of frequency-dependent DPs from in vivomeasurements of healthy and tumor rat breast tissues.Approach. Measurements were acquired over the 0.5-6 GHz frequency range.Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (cGAN) and Conditional VariationalAutoencoder (cVAE) were employed to learn the nonlinear mapping between the measuredS11 responses and the corresponding relative permittivity (ε') and dielectric loss factor(ε''). Furthermore, model performance was evaluated using dependency-preservingmetrics, including copula log-likelihood and Kendall's τ , together with regression metricssuch as root mean square error (RMSE), symmetric mean absolute percentage error(sMAPE), weighted mean absolute percentage error (wMAPE), and coefficient ofdetermination (R2). In addition, the estimated DP responses were fitted to a one-poleCole-Cole model using median normalized nonlinear least squares optimization to extractthe corresponding parameters (εs, ε∞, τ , α, σ).Main results. The lowest RMSE values for healthy and tumor tissues were 0.98 and 2.90,achieved by the cVAE and cGAN models, respectively. The mean absolute percentagedeviations, ∆(εc), between the Cole-Cole-fitted and reference DPs were 2.99% for healthytissues and 5.05% for tumor tissues.Significance. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of generative AI-based,non-iterative DP reconstruction directly from in vivo OECP measurements.

articles.title: OpenTOPAS-SPECT: an extension for full-physics clinical and preclinical SPECT simulation.
articles.abstract: Single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) simulations must resolve collimator transport, detector energy deposition, and low-efficiency projection formation within one model. General transport codes leave users to build the imaging components, whereas dedicated SPECT codes offer efficient camera models with less freedom to represent new systems. We developed OpenTOPAS-SPECT to bring projection-domain SPECT simulation into the declarative parameter-file workflow of OpenTOPAS.Approach: We added parametric parallel-hole, converging, pinhole, multi-pinhole, and slit-slat collimators; sodium-iodide and cadmium-zinc-telluride detector configurations; energy-resolved and forced-detection scorers; native decay-chain sources; and an evidence-graded library of 14 camera presets. We tested preset construction, multi-view consistency, and variance reduction, and benchmarked projection-domain quantities against measured, independent-code, and analytic references.Main results: At 140.5 keV and 10 cm from the collimator face, the Siemens Symbia low-energy high-resolution configuration gave 7.49 × 10-5 counts per decay, or 0.82 of the measured 9.1 × 10-5. GE collimator sensitivities were 1.08 to 1.15× the SIMIND range midpoints, while the 364.5 keV low-to-high-energy sensitivity ratio was 59.5 versus 67.7. Planar point-spread widths were 4% to 9% below analytic geometric resolution from 5 to 30 cm. In this Symbia LEHR point-source geometry, forced detection reached matched precision 6.9× faster than full transport and reproduced its absolute sensitivity to 1% without calibration. Across 20 configurations (five collimators, 113 keV to 1 MeV), forced detection stayed within 4% of full transport while septa carried up to a fifth of the signal, but fell 7% to 25% below it where they carried 25% or more. The release-gating suite ran all 23 example decks and built all 14 presets.Significance: OpenTOPAS-SPECT provides reusable SPECT components within the OpenTOPAS parameter system, with bounded projection-domain benchmarks for the first stable public release. The evidence supports the tested configurations and observables; reconstructed-image accuracy and broader system coverage remain untested.

articles.title: Cramér-Rao lower bound for spectral propagation-based x-ray phase-contrast imaging.
articles.abstract: Objective:Spectral x-ray phase-contrast imaging (XPCI) is a promising emerging method for quantitative phase retrieval. With an energy-discriminating detector, the independent measurements needed for quantitative phase retrieval or material decomposition can be acquired in a single shot. The existing Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB) model for attenuation-based spectral imaging, however, cannot capture the spatially distributed phase information associated with propagation-based (PB) XPCI. In this work, we develop a generalized CRLB framework for spectral PB-XPCI.Approach:The PB-XPCI forward model was formulated for nonideal, polychromatic photon-counting detector measurements. Two-material toy models were constructed with simple edge geometry to parallel the attenuation-based single-ray CRLB, with Poisson Fisher information computed over both energy-resolved and spatially distributed detector measurements. The conventional single-ray and proposed single-edge CRLBs were compared for ideal dual-monoenergy acquisitions. The single-edge model was then used to optimize detector energy thresholds for a nonideal 30-kVp polychromatic system, and CRLB predictions were validated against simulations.Main results:The single-edge model yielded substantially lower CRLBs relative to the fluence-matched single-ray model, while free-space propagation provided additional energy-dependent improvements. For the idealized monoenergetic single-edge model, the CRLB for each basis material was minimized when both measurements used the same energy, indicating that spatial measurements supplied sufficient independent information for material decomposition. For the polychromatic system, the CRLB exhibited material-dependent optimal energy thresholds, which shifted with the number of available energy bins. The single-edge and 2D-geometry CRLB models identified similar optimal energy thresholds within 0.1-1.9 keV, while simulated maximum-likelihood thickness estimates closely approached the CRLB with mean variance ratios of 1.006-1.020.Significance:The proposed CRLB model retains the interpretability of the familiar attenuation-based model while including propagation-based phase information, providing a useful theoretical foundation for evaluation and optimization of emerging spectral PB-XPCI systems as well as proposed phase retrieval and material decomposition algorithms.

articles.title: AI-accelerated compressed sensing and deep learning reconstruction for colon MRI: prospective validation of image quality and preliminary assessment of staging accuracy versus contrast-enhanced CT.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To prospectively validate an AI-accelerated MRI protocol combining L₁-regularized compressed sensing and deep learning reconstruction for colon cancer staging, compared with contrast-enhanced CT (CECT). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-center study (August 2022-April 2024) enrolled 132 patients with pathologically confirmed colon cancer who underwent both 3.0-T non-contrast MRI and CECT within 1 week. Patients unable to complete an MRI were excluded. MRI sequences included T1- and T2-weighted imaging and diffusion-weighted imaging. Image quality was assessed using a 4-point Likert scale, alongside quantitative analysis of contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) and edge rise distance (ERD). Surgical pathology correlation was available for 33 cases. Five radiologists independently reviewed the images. RESULTS: Among 153 matched examination pairs from 132 patients (mean age, 58 ± 11 years), AI-MRI outperformed CECT in both qualitative and quantitative measures. MRI yielded higher image quality scores (4 [IQR 3-4] vs. 3 [IQR 3-3]), improved CNR (5.5 [IQR 4.2-7.0] vs. 1.3 [IQR 0.7-2.2]), and reduced ERD (1.6 mm [IQR 1.2-2.8] vs. 3.7 mm [IQR 2.8-5.0]). MRI provided superior peritoneal sharpness (75.8%) and colonic wall visualization (100%), and superior or equivalent tumor conspicuity (92.2%) and nodal assessment (86.9%), whereas CECT demonstrated better artifact control (45.1%). In preliminary analyses, MRI achieved higher T-staging accuracy (78.8% vs. 30.3%) and N-staging specificity (93.3% vs. 13.3%). CONCLUSION: The AI-accelerated MRI protocol significantly outperformed CECT in image quality and preliminary staging accuracy for colon cancer evaluation while eliminating radiation exposure. KEY POINTS: Question Can an AI-accelerated MRI protocol provide superior image quality and staging performance compared with contrast-enhanced CT, which has limited diagnostic accuracy for colon cancer staging? Findings AI-accelerated MRI using L₁-regularized compressed sensing and deep learning reconstruction achieved superior image quality and higher preliminary staging accuracy than contrast-enhanced CT. Critical Relevance Statement AI-accelerated MRI improves image quality and staging confidence without radiation exposure, supporting its potential to enhance preoperative assessment and clinical decision-making in colon cancer.

articles.title: Deep learning-based quantification of CT changes after 1 year of pirfenidone treatment as a prognostic marker in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the prognostic value of changes in deep learning-based CT quantification following 1 year of pirfenidone treatment in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study included patients with IPF who received at least 1 year of pirfenidone between September 2009 and March 2022 at two hospitals. The extent of normal lung and fibrosis (sum of reticular opacity and honeycombing) was quantified on baseline and 1-year follow-up chest CT scans using a deep learning-based tool, and the changes were calculated. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality or lung transplantation; the secondary outcome was a ≥ 10% absolute decline in forced vital capacity (FVC) occurring after the 1-year follow-up. Associations between changes in CT quantification and these outcomes were assessed using Cox proportional hazards regression analyses. RESULTS: A total of 436 patients (341 men; mean age, 69.8 years) were included. Greater preservation of normal lung extent over 1 year was associated with a lower risk of the composite outcome (adjusted hazard ratio (HR) per 5% increase: 0.90; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.85, 0.96; p < 0.001), whereas increases in fibrosis extent were associated with a higher risk (adjusted HR per 5% increase: 1.16, 95% CI: 1.06, 1.27, p = 0.002). Regarding the secondary outcome of ≥ 10% absolute FVC decline, only the change in fibrosis extent remained a significant predictor (adjusted HR per 5% increase: 1.26, 95% CI: 1.09, 1.45, p = 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Changes in deep learning-based CT quantification results over 1 year of pirfenidone treatment demonstrated significant prognostic value in patients with IPF. KEY POINTS: Question Disease progression and mortality in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) continue to occur unpredictably beyond 1 year of pirfenidone treatment. Findings Changes in deep learning-based quantification of normal lung and fibrosis extent after 1 year of pirfenidone treatment were significant prognostic predictors. Critical relevance statement Incorporating 1-year changes in deep learning-based CT quantification improves prognostication of mortality, lung transplantation, and lung function decline, supporting more individualized risk stratification in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.

articles.title: Automatic generation of training data from dual-energy CT scans: a new approach to train renal vessel segmentation models.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the feasibility of automatic training data generation using virtual non-contrast (VNC) images of dual-energy CT and to evaluate the performance of medical segmentation models trained on auto-generated data. METHODS: Training images were generated from contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) scans using VNC algorithm. Corresponding training labels were generated from iodine-density images via intensity thresholding. The paired VNC images and labels constituted the dataset (791 cases in total) for training non-enhanced CT (NECT) segmentation models. We attempted to train segmentation models with VNC images alone, as well as the combination of VNC and real NECT images. RESULTS: Models trained with auto-generated data effectively performed renal vein segmentation on NECT images, achieving Dice score of 69.60%. It identified 100% (70/70) vein main trunks and 54.5% (6/11) accessory veins in the test set. The models' performance on artery segmentation was not satisfactory, with Dice score of 44.56%. It only identified 41.4% (29/70) artery main trunks and 4.54% (1/22) accessory arteries. However, the combination of generated data and labeled data greatly improved model's artery Dice to 71.23%. Combined model identified 100% (70/70) vein main trunks, 98.6% (69/70) artery main trunks, 68.2% (15/22) accessory arteries and 63.6% (7/11) accessory veins. Its accessory artery detection is significantly higher than the model trained with labeled data (15/22 vs. 5/22, p < 0.01), closing the gap with human radiologist (15/22 vs. 18/22, p = 0.250). CONCLUSION: VNC and Iodine-density images can be utilized to automatically generate training data for segmentation models. This pipeline shows promise for training segmentation models on NECT images.

articles.title: T2-weighted MRI-based radiomics for preoperative prediction of homologous recombination deficiency status in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to explore the feasibility of T2-weighted imaging (T2WI) - based radiomics in preoperative prediction of homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) status in patients with high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), and to establish a non-invasive approach for guiding individualized treatment planning. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 133 patients with pathologically confirmed HGSOC who underwent MRI scan (T2WI, T1-contrast enhanced) were retrospectively enrolled in this study. All patients were stratified into HRD-positive and HRD-negative group. These 133 patients (41 in HRD-negative group and 92 in HRD-positive group) were randomly allocated to a training set (n = 93) and a validation set (n = 40) at a 7:3 ratio. Three different models were constructed and evaluated: clinical characteristics only (clinical model); T2WI-radiomics features only (radiomics model); and a combination of them all (combined model). The predictive performance was evaluated using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and area under the curves (AUCs) were compared using the DeLong test. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA) were applied to validate the clinical-radiomic combined model. RESULTS: In the training set, the combined model achieved the best performance (AUC = 0.889; all P > 0.05). The radiomics model achieved predictive performance comparable to the clinical model (AUC of 0.762 vs. 0.790; P = 0.676). In the validation set, the combined model performed significantly better than the clinical or radiomics model (AUCs of 0.853 vs. 0.805 vs. 0.706; all P > 0.05). DCA demonstrated that the combined model achieved superior net benefit across a wide range of threshold probabilities compared with the clinical and radiomics models alone. CONCLUSIONS: Our research demonstrated that the combined model achieved the optimal predictive performance. It is feasible to apply radiomics to predict HRD status of HGSOC patients, which can further assist clinicians in formulating individualized treatment strategies.

articles.title: CT-fibrosis score: development and internal validation for identifying advanced fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Advanced fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) involves metabolic and anatomic remodeling beyond the liver. We developed and internally validated an interpretable CT-based score integrating abdominal body-composition and organ measurements and compared it with the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index. METHODS: We retrospectively studied 151 patients with biopsy-confirmed MASLD (86 advanced [F3-F4], 65 early-stage [F0-F2] fibrosis). Deep learning-based segmentation quantified abdominal adipose tissue, skeletal muscle, bone, liver, and spleen measurements. The CT-Fibrosis Score was developed using repeated (50×) stratified 5-fold cross-validation, with imputation, standardization, and feature selection confined to each training fold and inner 5-fold cross-validation for hyperparameter selection. Performance was based on out-of-fold predictions and compared with FIB-4 using the DeLong test. Sensitivity analyses addressed missing data, age dependence, and ascites. RESULTS: Four features were consistently selected: age, bone-to-abdominal-cavity volume ratio, visceral adipose tissue (VAT) density, and spleen index. The CT-Fibrosis Score achieved an out-of-fold AUC of 0.77 (95% CI 0.69-0.85). Among 141 patients with an available FIB-4 score, no significant difference was detected between the CT-Fibrosis Score (AUC 0.76) and FIB-4 (AUC 0.79; difference - 0.03, 95% CI - 0.11 to + 0.04; p = 0.37); this comparison was not powered for non-inferiority. Adding the CT-Fibrosis Score to FIB-4 did not improve discrimination (AUC 0.80 vs. 0.79; difference + 0.003, 95% CI - 0.04 to + 0.05; p = 0.90), with the confidence interval excluding an improvement greater than approximately 0.05. CONCLUSION: The CT-Fibrosis Score achieved moderate discrimination for advanced fibrosis but did not improve discrimination when added to FIB-4. External validation in an unselected population undergoing CT for non-hepatic indications is required before any opportunistic application.

articles.title: Prognostic value of dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI and plasma angiogenic markers for survival outcomes in HPV-negative oropharyngeal carcinoma treated with concurrent chemoradiotherapy.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) enables non-invasive assessment of tumour vascularity, while circulating angiogenic factors may reflect tumour-associated angiogenic activity. We investigated whether DCE-MRI perfusion parameters and plasma angiogenic factors measured before and early during concurrent chemoradiotherapy (cCRT) are associated with survival in human papillomavirus (HPV)-negative oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC). METHODS: In this prospective single-centre study, 24 patients with locally advanced HPV-negative OPSCC treated with cCRT were analysed. DCE-MRI perfusion parameters (Ktrans, Kep, Ve, iAUC) were analysed at baseline and early intra-treatment (20 Gy), while plasma angiogenic factors (vascular endothelial growth factor [VEGF], connective tissue growth factor, platelet-derived growth factor-AB, angiogenin, endostatin, and thrombospondin-1) were analysed at baseline, early intra-treatment and post-treatment (10-12 weeks). Disease-specific survival (DSS) was assessed using univariable Cox regression (hazard ratios [HRs] per 1-SD) and Kaplan-Meier analysis with false-discovery-rate correction. RESULTS: Seven patients died of the index cancer. Higher baseline Ktrans (HR per 1-SD 0.30, p = 0.031) and higher early intra-treatment plasma VEGF (HR 0.37, p = 0.043) were nominally associated with better DSS; VEGF also showed separation in Kaplan-Meier analysis (3-year DSS 92% vs. 36%, log-rank p = 0.016). Effect estimates were similar after exploratory adjustment for tumour volume but attenuated after adjustment for stage. No association remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction, and the early VEGF association partly overlapped with local treatment response. CONCLUSION: In this exploratory analysis, baseline DCE-MRI perfusion (Ktrans) and plasma VEGF showed hypothesis-generating associations with DSS in HPV-negative OPSCC. As no association survived multiplicity correction, these findings require validation in larger independent cohorts.

articles.title: The "Pearl Sign": A conventional MRI feature for distinguishing brain metastasis from glioblastoma and primary CNS lymphoma.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate the diagnostic value of the Pearl Sign for differentiating brain metastasis from glioblastoma and primary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL). METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 281 adult patients with histopathologically confirmed brain metastasis (n = 88), glioblastoma (n = 126), or PCNSL (n = 67) who underwent pretreatment MRI between January 2016 and July 2026. Two blinded neuroradiologists independently assessed the Pearl Sign, defined as the presence of ≥ 5 peripheral cystic foci, and conventional MRI features. Univariable one-vs-rest logistic regression with Holm-Bonferroni correction was followed by multivariable logistic regression to identify independent predictors. A subgroup analysis was additionally performed in patients with solitary lesions. RESULTS: The Pearl Sign was present in 60.2% of brain metastases, compared with 6.3% of glioblastomas and 1.5% of PCNSLs (P < .001). It was a​ strong​ independent predictor of brain metastasis (adjusted OR, 25.98; 95% CI, 11.11-60.75; P < .001). Smooth margin (adjusted OR, 4.84; P < .001) and greater peritumoral edema size (adjusted OR, 1.43 per 10-mm increase; P = .004) were additional independent predictors, whereas homogeneous enhancement was inversely associated with brain metastasis (adjusted OR, 0.42; P = .035). The final four-variable model achieved an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.883, with 76.1% sensitivity, 88.6% specificity, and 84.7% accuracy, outperforming the corresponding model without the Pearl Sign (AUC, 0.777; accuracy, 71.3%). In patients with solitary lesions, the Pearl Sign-containing model demonstrated even higher diagnostic performance, with an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.916, 79.7% sensitivity, 93.6% specificity, and 88.8% accuracy. CONCLUSION: The Pearl Sign is a strong independent predictor of brain metastasis and provides incremental diagnostic value beyond established MRI features. Incorporating this readily assessable sign may improve differentiation of brain metastasis from glioblastoma and PCNSL.

articles.title: Evaluation of the relationship between the anatomical and morphometric characteristics of the sphenoid sinus in the paediatric population.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: The aim was to analyse the morphological characteristics of the sphenoid sinus in the paediatric population and the possible effects of sex and age on the prevalence of pneumatization. METHODS: Patients in the 0-16 age group were determined as the paediatric group, and patients 16+ years of age were determined as the control group. Sphenoid sinus measurements and pneumatization classification were performed by two maxillofacial radiologists. Sphenoid sinus pneumatizations are divided into three groups: sellar, clival, and lateral. RESULTS: Types of right lateral pneumatization show significant differences between age groups (P=0.023). Lat-D type was significantly more prevalent in control group, while Lat-B type was observed only in the paediatric group. Like the right side, left lateral pneumatization types also showed statistically significant differences between age groups (P=0.013). Lat-D type is significantly more common in control group, while Lat-C is more frequently observed in the paediatric group. In terms of symmetry, there is a borderline significant difference between age groups (P≈0.05). While the height of the sphenoid sinus exhibited a weak positive correlation with the length of the optic chiasm (R=0.273, P<0.001), the anteroposterior length and width of the sphenoid sinus both demonstrated moderate positive correlations with the intercarotid distance (R=0.333 and R=0.435, P<0.001). CONCLUSION: Lateral pneumatization type showed significant age-related changes. Optic chiasm length correlated with sphenoid sinus height, while intercarotid distance correlated with both sphenoid sinus anteroposterior length and width.

articles.title: Calcified foraminal metastasis from ovarian low-grade serous carcinoma mimicking a nerve sheath tumor.
articles.abstract: Ovarian low-grade serous carcinoma (OLGSC) is an uncommon subtype of epithelial ovarian cancer, characterized by an indolent clinical course with potential for late local recurrence and metastatic disease. Musculoskeletal involvement is rare. We report a case of late OLGSC metastasis presenting as a slowly growing, thoracic foraminal mass in a 55-year-old woman, 33 years after initial cancer treatment. Rising CA-125 levels prompted 18F-FDG PET/CT, which revealed an FDG-avid mass in the left T9-T10 neural foramen (SUVmax 6.6). CT demonstrated foraminal widening and intralesional calcifications, while MRI showed a dumbbell-shaped mass extending into the epidural space and left costovertebral region, with heterogeneous signal intensity and mild diffuse heterogeneous enhancement. Retrospective review of a CT examination performed 12 years earlier revealed a smaller foraminal mass without visible calcifications. Given its location and morphology, the lesion initially suggested a nerve sheath tumor, while the presence of calcifications also raised the possibility of a chondroid lesion. Although nonspecific, calcifications are recognized in primary and metastatic OLGSC. The combination of increased FDG uptake and the patient's oncologic history, raised suspicion of metastatic disease. Image-guided biopsy confirmed metastatic OLGSC with psammoma bodies. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported case of OLGSC metastasis presenting as a slowly progressive, calcified paravertebral and foraminal mas mimicking a nerve sheath tumor. This case emphasizes the need for careful evaluation of atypical masses in patients with a history of cancer, even decades after initial treatment, and the importance of biopsy for diagnostic confirmation.

articles.title: Free-breathing fast abdominal simultaneous T1, T2, PD and B1 mapping via deep learning reconstruction.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Multi-parametric quantitative MRI (mqMRI) enables non-invasive tissue characterization and holds significant clinical value in abdominal imaging. Conventional methods are restricted by long acquisition times and motion artifacts induced by physiological processes and irregular breathing, leading to registration errors between sequential acquisitions. PURPOSE: To develop and evaluate a framework for abdominal quantitative imaging under free-breathing conditions with reduced scan time and improved robustness to motion. METHODS: A novel framework integrating the longitudinal magnetization-controlled multiple overlapping-echo detachment (LMC-MOLED) sequence with synthetic data-driven deep learning reconstruction was proposed. To generate the synthetic dataset for training, a respiratory motion model combining global and local displacement vector fields was developed, ensuring temporal alignment with the inter-phase intervals of LMC-MOLED acquisitions. By applying interpolation to the original template, virtual imaging objects were generated to simulate respiratory-induced deformations while preserving anatomical textures, tissue boundaries, and inter-slice correlations. These objects were subsequently processed with MRI Bloch simulation to generate the final synthetic dataset, which was used to train a BGA-Multi-UNet architecture for motion correction and improved quantitative accuracy. RESULTS: The proposed framework enabled simultaneous mapping of T1, T2, proton density, and B1 under free-breathing conditions. With a 5-slice interleaved acquisition, the average acquisition time was reduced to approximately one second per slice without the need for respiratory gating. Both numerical and in vivo experiments demonstrated high accuracy and repeatability, with image quality comparable to conventional breath-hold acquisitions while mitigating motion-induced artifacts. CONCLUSION: This framework offers a rapid and reliable solution for multi-parametric abdominal imaging under free-breathing conditions. The combination of synthetic motion modeling with deep learning reconstruction enables accurate quantitative mapping with effective motion correction, offering potential clinical benefits for efficient and robust abdominal magnetic resonance imaging.

articles.title: Impact of correlated PBPK parameters on intra-patient global sensitivity analysis in molecular radiotherapy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models integrated into digital twins provide a robust framework for optimizing individualized molecular radiotherapy (MRT). Nevertheless, uncertainties in PBPK-model-derived dosimetry can compromise the reliability of dosimetry-guided treatment planning and individualized therapy decisions. PURPOSE: This study employs intra-patient global sensitivity analysis (GSA) to assess the influence of uncertainty and correlations among PBPK model parameters on estimated kidney and tumor absorbed doses (ADs) in prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted theragnostics. METHODS: Data from 10 patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who underwent pre-therapeutic [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-I&T PET/CT and a cycle of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-I&T therapy, followed by post-therapeutic SPECT/CT scans at Days 1 and 4 post-injection, were analyzed. A previously established whole-body PBPK model for PSMA-targeted radionuclide therapy was used as the baseline model. Fifteen model parameters, their standard errors, and inter-parameter correlations were estimated by fitting to measured time-activity data and subsequently evaluated using intra-patient GSA based on the Kucherenko method implemented in UQLab. In one approach, correlations were ignored to identify the direct influences of uncertainty in input parameters on ADs. In a second approach, correlations were included to reflect realistic parameter distributions and to capture indirect effects arising from parameter interdependencies. Pharmacokinetics were simulated to estimate therapeutic kidney and tumor ADs as well as main- and total-effect indices (  S i , S i T )   . Sensitivity indices, ADs, and their associated uncertainty metrics were compared between scenarios with and without parameter correlations. RESULTS: Including parameter correlations in the GSA yielded kidney ADs of 4.2 Gy [3.0-7.2 Gy] (median [min-max]) with standard deviations (SDs) of 0.5 Gy [0.4-0.9 Gy] and tumor ADs of 10.1 Gy [2.0-26.8 Gy] with SDs of 1.7 Gy [0.6-3.4 Gy]. Neglecting correlations resulted in significantly higher uncertainties in ADs, by a factor of 1.2 [1.0-1.8] for both kidneys and tumors. Kidney ADs were most sensitive to kidney receptor density (  S i = 0.3  [ 0.1 -  0.6 ] ,   S i T = 0.7  [ 0.6 - 0.8 ]   ) and to the filtered fraction of renal blood flow ( S i = 0.2  [ 0.1 - 0.3 ] ,   S i T = 0.3  [ 0.1 - 0.4 ] )   . Tumor ADs were most affected by tumor receptor density (  S i = 0.7  [ 0.1 - 1.0 ] ,   S i T = 0.8  [ 0.3 - 1.0 ]   ). The involvement of parameter correlations did not alter the identification of the parameters most influential on AD estimates and further reduced computational runtime. CONCLUSIONS: Incorporating parameter correlations into intra-patient GSA reduced the estimated uncertainty associated with ADs, underscoring the importance of preserving parameter dependencies when propagating uncertainty in PBPK-based individualized MRT. The identification of key PBPK parameters governing kidney and tumor ADs remained stable when including correlation, confirming the robustness of the underlying model structure.

articles.title: A multi-reader multi-case study comparing Breast Cancer Reading Efficiency and Accuracy in Screening with Tomosynthesis versus AI-assisted mammography.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Full-field digital mammography (FFDM) is the standard for breast cancer screening but has reduced sensitivity in dense breasts. Digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) improves cancer detection compared to 2D mammography but is limited by cost and longer reading times. Artificial intelligence (AI)-enhanced mammography has demonstrated improved sensitivity compared to 2D mammography. This study compares AI-enhanced 2D mammography (DM+AI) with DBT in recalling interval breast cancers (IBCs). METHODS: : A multi-reader, multi-case crossover study was conducted using the Emory BrEast Imaging Dataset, which includes paired FFDM and DBT images with biopsy-proven outcomes. Six radiologists reviewed 53 IBC and 53 screen-detected cancer (SDC) cases, with random assignment to DM+AI or DBT, followed by crossover after a washout period. Primary outcomes included recall rate of IBCs. Secondary outcomes included recall rate of SDCs, interpretation time, and subgroup analysis by breast density. RESULTS: : For IBCs, DM+AI and DBT demonstrated similar recall rates (41.5% vs 40.9%) and detection rates (14.8% vs 11.9%). DM+AI identified more non-invasive (31.5% vs 13.0%) and mass-forming (61.0% vs 21.8%) cancers. For SDCs, recall and detection rates were comparable across modalities. In fatty breasts, recall was higher with DM+AI (91.7% vs 50.0%), while DBT performed better in extremely dense breasts. DM+AI enabled faster interpretation, averaging 24.1 seconds less per case. CONCLUSION: : AI-enhanced 2D mammography demonstrated comparable performance to DBT with shorter interpretation times, supporting a stratified screening approach. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This study is the first direct comparison of AI-enhanced mammography and digital breast tomosynthesis for IBC detection.

articles.title: Comparative Study of Dual-energy X‑ray Absorptiometry versus Multislice Computed Tomography for Vertebral Height Measurement.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study investigates the discrepancies between two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) imaging-based approaches for vertebral height assessment. METHODS: Lumbar spine CT scans and dual-energy X‑ray absorptiometry (DXA) studies within 6 months were reviewed. Vertebral fracture assessment was performed by converting CT-measured height ratios into Genant grades using three methods: conventional (A), consensus (B), and global search (C). Dataset 1 included 34 patients (191 vertebrae; 1,302 CT slices) with CT and DXA; Dataset 2 included 114 patients with CT only. RESULTS: No significant difference was observed between Method A and DXA-based grading (p = 0.33). In contrast, Methods B and C significantly differed from DXA (p < 0.001, both). Discrepancies were greatest for vertebrae graded as 1 by Method A (98 and 166 vertebrae reclassified by Methods B and C, respectively). Compared with Method A, Method B revealed greater height reductions in Grades 0, 1, and 2 vertebrae by 9.00, 9.13, and 13.75 percentage points, respectively. For Method C, these reductions were 10.71, 10.14, and 12.35 percentage points, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Compared with DXA, continuous sagittal CT images improved detection of greatest vertebral height loss, especially for Grade 1 reductions. When applying 2D criteria to CT scans, clinicians should be cautious of a tendency to overestimate vertebral height loss. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This first study demonstrates that the 3D method yields vertebral height reduction 10.84 percentage points greater than the 2D method. Therefore, overestimation of vertebral height reduction on CT should be considered when radiological classification criteria are applied.

articles.title: Reliability-weighted patch learning for synthetic CT reconstruction in head and neck adaptive radiotherapy: A proof-of-concept study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is essential for adaptive radiotherapy (ART) but is limited by poor image quality. Existing deep learning methods for synthetic CT (sCT) generation face a critical trade-off: diffusion models offer high fidelity but are impractically slow, while fast-inference networks often lack structural accuracy and optimization stability. PURPOSE: To develop HQ-PatchNet, a reliability-driven deep learning framework designed to improve CBCT-to-sCT image quality while maintaining rapid inference speed for online ART workflows. METHODS: HQ-PatchNet utilizes a vision transformer (ViT)-integrated CycleGAN architecture. It introduces a reliability-driven, SSIM-based selective patch weighting mechanism controlled by a temperature decay schedule. This dynamically suppresses artifact-dominated regions and focuses optimization on anatomically reliable structures. The model was evaluated on 304 paired head-and-neck (HN) scans against conventional networks and recent diffusion models using quantitative metrics (MAE, SSIM, NCC, PSNR), computational speed, and clinical dosimetric accuracy (3D gamma index, 2%/2 mm). RESULTS: HQ-PatchNet improved image quality, reducing Mean Absolute Error (MAE) from 44.81 ± 11.24 HU to 11.85 ± 4.31 HU and achieving an SSIM of 0.960 ± 0.055, comparable to state-of-the-art diffusion models. Inference required only 6.42 ± 1.71 s per volume, compared to > 15 min for diffusion approaches. The model reduced severe metal and truncation artifacts, and representative qualitative assessment suggested visually consistent sCT generation under interfractional anatomical variation. Dosimetric assessment of complex HN IMRT plans yielded a high average gamma passing rate of 99.32 ± 0.56%. CONCLUSIONS: HQ-PatchNet provides a computationally efficient and clinically promising approach for daily CBCT-guided online ART by improving CBCT-to-sCT image quality while maintaining rapid inference speed. Further contour-based, multi-institutional, and multi-site validation remains necessary to confirm its broader clinical utility.

articles.title: Evidence of White Matter R2* Homogenization After Formalin Fixation.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Disentangling intrinsic susceptibility-driven R2* characteristics in white matter (WM) from fixation-related effects using in vivo, postmortem (PM) in situ, and formalin-fixed PM ex situ MRI. METHODS: DTI and multi-echo gradient-echo MRI were acquired in vivo, PM in situ and PM ex situ. PM cases included neurologically healthy individuals and patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Voxel-wise R2* values were obtained using a mono-exponential fit and evaluated both as whole WM averages and according to WM fiber-to-field orientation. For the PM ex situ orientation-dependency analysis, PM ex situ R2* data were registered to the corresponding in situ DTI acquisition. Averaged as well as orientation-dependent R2* profiles were pooled across WM and compared across conditions. RESULTS: Whole WM averaged and orientation-dependent R2* values differed across in vivo, PM in situ, and PM ex situ conditions. No differences were observed between PM in situ healthy and PM in situ ALS cases. Compared with in vivo measurements, both PM conditions showed elevated whole WM averaged R2* values and reduced orientation dependency, with the strongest R2* anisotropy in vivo and nearly absent orientation dependency in the PM ex situ condition. CONCLUSION: While orientation-dependent R2* is reduced but preserved in unfixed PM in situ tissue, it is largely eliminated after prolonged formalin fixation without rehydration, likely due to microstructural reorganization and protein cross-linking. Collectively, these findings indicate that orientation-dependent R2* measured in fixed tissue has limited translational validity, while underscoring its sensitivity to intact microstructural organization in vivo and in unfixed PM tissue.

articles.title: Rep2Rep-Shuffle: Shuffled Repetition-to-Repetition Learning for Noise-Adaptive Self-Supervised MRI Denoising.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: MRI applications with low SNR, such as non-proton imaging and low-field imaging, often require multiple signal averages to achieve adequate image quality at the cost of longer scan times. This work proposes Rep2Rep-Shuffle, a self-supervised learning framework that improves MRI denoising performance in repeated-acquisition imaging with limited training datasets. METHODS: Rep2Rep-Shuffle extends our previously proposed repetition-to-repetition learning (Rep2Rep)-based self-supervised denoising approach with a new shuffled repetition pairing strategy. Instead of using a fixed split between training input and target repetitions, different repetition combinations are randomly generated during training epochs for each dataset, which increases the effective training space when training datasets are limited. In addition, the framework also extends from slice-wise 2D to 3D denoising by exploiting correlations across all spatial dimensions. The proposed method was tested in vivo using sodium MRI and further validated using synthetic noisy MRI datasets. Different training strategies for both 2D and 3D denoising were compared. RESULTS: In vivo sodium MRI results demonstrated improved denoising and better preservation of anatomical structures with 3D Rep2Rep-Shuffle compared with fixed pairing (Rep2Rep) and 2D denoising. Reader evaluation further confirmed that 3D Rep2Rep-Shuffle received higher scores for different assessment categories. In synthetic experiments, 3D Rep2Rep-Shuffle achieved the best performance among self-supervised methods and approached the performance of supervised learning. CONCLUSION: Rep2Rep-Shuffle outperforms Rep2Rep for MRI denoising by increasing training diversity through shuffled repetition pairing and by leveraging volumetric spatial correlations. The method is particularly suited for low-SNR MRI applications that acquire multiple repetitions but have limited training datasets.

articles.title: Accelerated MR Elastography Using Learned Neural Network Representation.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop a deep-learning method for achieving fast high-resolution MR elastography from highly undersampled data without the need for high-quality training datasets. METHODS: We first reframed the deep neural network representation as a nonlinear extension of the linear subspace model, then used it to represent and reconstruct MRE image repetitions from undersampled k-space data. A multi-level k-space consistency loss was proposed to learn the network weights and mitigate overfitting. To further enhance reconstruction quality, phase-contrast specific magnitude and phase priors were incorporated, namely the similarity of anatomical structures and smoothness of wave-induced harmonic displacement. The network was trained in a self-supervised manner with empirically fixed iterations. Experiments were conducted using one multi-slice spin-echo and two 3D gradient-echo spiral MRE datasets. RESULTS: Compared to conventional linear subspace-based approaches, the nonlinear network representation method produced superior image reconstruction with suppressed artifacts and noise from a single in-plane spiral arm per MRE repetition, yielding stiffness estimation (e.g., from a 3D GRE sequence at 2 mm resolution within 1 min, R = 10) comparable to that obtained from fully sampled data. CONCLUSION: This work demonstrated the feasibility of using deep network representations to model and reconstruct MRE images from highly undersampled data, a nonlinear extension of the subspace-based approach. Future work will include validation on a larger and more diverse cohort of subjects to further assess its robustness and generalizability.

articles.title: Recursive partitioning analysis model based on 18F-FDG PET/CT metabolic parameters for recurrent or metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma treated with PD-1 inhibitors and chemotherapy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: We aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of baseline 18F-FDG PET/CT metabolic parameters and to construct a risk stratification model for recurrent/metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (rmNPC) patients receiving first-line PD-1 inhibitors plus chemotherapy. METHODS: A total of 148 rmNPC patients from two centers were included. Whole-body total lesion glycolysis (wTLG), whole-body metabolic tumor volume (wMTV), and maximal standardized uptake values (SUVmax) were assessed. Predictive performance was evaluated via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, while progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were identified using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses. A recursive partitioning analysis (RPA) model was subsequently developed and validated for risk stratification. RESULTS: Lower baseline wTLG and wMTV were associated with better response and longer PFS and OS, with wTLG showing the highest predictive power (AUC = 0.776). The RPA model stratified patients into low-risk (low wTLG), medium-risk (high wTLG without liver metastasis), and high-risk (high wTLG with liver metastasis) groups, demonstrating significantly different median PFS (30.7, 15.9, 7.1 months) and OS (43.7, 29.9, 14.7 months; all p < 0.001), and achieving an AUC of 0.839 for predicting 3-year disease progression. Radiotherapy improved survival outcomes in the low-risk group but not in the high-risk group. Analysis of 213 individual lesions revealed heterogeneous responses, with lymph node metastases showing the best response and liver metastases the poorest. CONCLUSION: Baseline PET/CT metabolic parameters, particularly wTLG, serve as powerful predictors of survival in NPC patients receiving chemoimmunotherapy. The wTLG-based RPA model provides a robust tool for risk stratification and holds promise for guiding individualized clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Skull-Base Synthetic CT from Brain MRI: Development, Independent-Center Validation, and Radiologist Evaluation.
articles.abstract: We developed and evaluated a deep learning pipeline for skull-base synthetic computed tomography (sCT) generation from routine non-contrast T1-weighted and T2-weighted brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), focusing on clinically relevant bony anatomy for neurosurgical and radiotherapy workflows. We retrospectively collected 184 manually registered T1/T2/CT triplets for training and internal validation (166/18 split) and 43 cases from a second center for independent-center validation. A three-dimensional Swin-UNETR generator was trained with bone-weighted multiscale reconstruction, perceptual, and adversarial losses. Two board-certified radiologists independently scored 16 skull-base structures, artifacts, and diagnostic acceptability on raw sCT in Hounsfield units (HU), without histogram matching; this blinded review was the primary endpoint. Acceptability was 76.7% for Rater 1 and 67.4% for Rater 2 (pooled 72.1%, cluster-robust 95% CI 58.5-82.6%), with mean structure scores from 2.67 to 4.85 out of 5. Raw sCT showed limited absolute HU calibration (global MAE 364 ± 50   HU, bone Dice 0.38 ± 0.09  ), with a compressed dynamic range in which air and soft tissue were overestimated and dense bone underestimated; histogram-matched outputs, reported as a secondary analysis, reached bone Dice 0.88 ± 0.03  and bone MAE 26.31 ± 5.03   HU. Halo artifacts were near-universal, and false-canal artifacts occurred in 21-30% of cases. The method shows promise as a radiation-free adjunct for skull-base visualization, but the present results do not support replacing dedicated CT for diagnostic, dosimetric, or physics-based applications.

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance and Calibration of AI Models for Thyroid Ultrasound Malignancy Classification: From TN5000 to ThyroidXL.
articles.abstract: We evaluated cross-dataset transportability of three frozen encoders for binary benign-versus-malignant thyroid ultrasound classification using expert-defined nodule regions and one external cohort. Logistic regression classifiers using DINOv2, TinyUSFM, and ResNet18 features were developed on 3500 TN5000 images, calibrated on 477 duplicate-clean validation images and tested on 958 images. External evaluation used maximum image scores from 2083 ThyroidXL images in 739 patients with cytological or histopathological outcomes. No external retraining, recalibration or threshold adjustment was performed. Additional analyses evaluated four classifiers, encoder-recommended preprocessing and calibration intercepts and slopes. Internal areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) were 0.9081 for TinyUSFM, 0.8946 for DINOv2, and 0.8896 for ResNet18. Primary external AUROCs were 0.8464 (95% confidence interval, 0.8164-0.8731), 0.7954, and 0.7833, respectively. Sensitivities at frozen high-sensitivity thresholds were 0.9972, 0.9717, and 0.9887, but specificities were 0.1736, 0.1891, and 0.1373. External calibration intercepts were negative; slopes were 0.891, 0.645, and 0.697. DINOv2 ranked first externally with four of five classifiers. With recommended preprocessing, ResNet18 ranked first numerically (0.8329 versus 0.8214 for DINOv2); their paired difference was inconclusive. Encoder rankings depended on the classifier and preprocessing. These results apply to the three evaluated implementations, not pretraining strategies generally. Transported patient scores overestimated malignancy and had low specificity. Prospective assessment is needed before clinical use.

articles.title: Vision Transformer-Based Automated Ordinal Grading of Supraspinatus Tendon Pathology and a Quantitative Faithfulness Audit of Attribution Maps in Shoulder MRI.
articles.abstract: Rotator cuff disorders, most often of the supraspinatus tendon, are a leading cause of shoulder pain, and magnetic resonance imaging is the reference modality. Grading their progression is subject to inter-reader variability, and automated systems for the task are expected to justify themselves through attribution maps. This study asks whether they do. Four Vision Transformer tiers spanning a 54-fold parameter range were trained under one searched configuration and averaged into an unweighted ensemble. On 694 regionally annotated sections from 276 shoulders in 264 patients, the ensemble reached 0.9130 accuracy (95% CI, 0.8406-0.9710) and a 0.9431 quadratic weighted kappa on a 69-section, patient-level held-out test subset. The four tiers differed by at most 0.0580, inside the 0.07 resolution limit, so any capacity effect is bounded below it rather than shown absent. Seven attribution methods from four mechanism families were scored against an occlusion reference. Occlusion placed 16.82 times chance mass on the annotated region, the attribution methods 1.15 to 13.90. Against a random ordering of the same cells, occlusion separated the deletion and insertion curves by 0.4773, a margin no method reached, and two methods beat this baseline on deletion but lost on insertion. The method closest to the reference kept a correlation of 0.977 with its own map after half the network was randomized. Repeating the audit under a Gaussian blur fill left the ranking of all eight arms unchanged. An attribution map offered as clinical evidence therefore requires interventional validation, with its perturbation and grid sensitivity reported.

articles.title: Contrast-Free ADC Intensity Features for Early Neurological Deterioration in Lacunar Infarction: An Exploratory Comparison with Perfusion Imaging and Deep Learning.
articles.abstract: Early neurological deterioration (END) affects approximately one in five patients with acute lacunar infarction and is associated with poor functional outcome. Hypoperfusion on contrast-enhanced perfusion MRI has been linked to END, but perfusion imaging requires intravenous contrast and is not part of the routine acute workup for minor stroke. We explored whether intensity features of non-contrast structural MRI carry information on END, using the visually classified pattern from a contrast-enhanced perfusion study in the same patients as a reference. We analyzed a prospectively collected single-center cohort of patients with acute lacunar infarction who underwent MRI within 24 h of symptom onset, including diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) mapping, fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR), and dynamic susceptibility contrast perfusion imaging. END was defined as an increase of ≥ 2 points on the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale within 72 h. One hundred patients with complete imaging and outcome data were included, of whom 20 (20.0%) developed END. Candidate predictors comprised intensity features of the infarct core and an 8-mm perilesional rim normalized to whole-brain intensity, 201 DWI texture features, and 22 clinical and laboratory variables. Models were evaluated by 10-times-repeated 5-fold stratified cross-validation with the decision threshold fixed at 0.5; feature selection and standardization were performed within training folds only. The visually classified perfusion pattern served as a contrast-based clinical benchmark. ADC intensity features discriminated END with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.699 (approximate patient-level 95% CI 0.56-0.84) and an area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.473 against a base rate of 0.200; at the fixed threshold, sensitivity was 52.0% and positive predictive value 27.9%. The perfusion pattern alone yielded a sensitivity of 70.0%, a specificity of 60.0% and a negative predictive value of 88.9% (balanced accuracy 0.650). The difference between the two predictors was small relative to the sampling uncertainty at 20 events, so neither superiority nor equivalence could be established. The strongest individual feature was the 75th percentile of normalized ADC within the infarct core (univariate AUC 0.702), with higher values in patients who deteriorated (median 0.615 versus 0.555, P = 0.005). Adding the perfusion pattern to the ADC features did not improve discrimination (AUC 0.665, 95% CI 0.645-0.684). The signal was confined to the ADC map: models built on DWI or FLAIR intensity alone performed below chance (AUC 0.463 and 0.453). More complex models did not reach the ADC model at this sample size: 201 DWI texture features reached an AUC of 0.566, clinical and laboratory variables at best 0.625, and an end-to-end 2.5D ResNet-18 0.404 with random initialization, 0.482 with ImageNet pretraining and 0.611 for a small network sized for the data. In this exploratory single-center study, ADC intensity features obtained without contrast were associated with END in acute lacunar infarction, with discrimination similar in magnitude to the contrast-enhanced perfusion benchmark; the cohort was too small to establish equivalence, and threshold-level performance is insufficient to guide monitoring. Texture analysis and deep learning could not be adequately trained with 20 events, so their relative merit cannot be judged. ADC appears to be the informative non-contrast sequence; the findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger, multicenter cohorts.

articles.title: DINOv3-SAM: Fusing Semantic and Anatomical Foundation Models for Robust Medical Image Classification.
articles.abstract: Robust medical image classification remains a persistent challenge due to heterogeneous acquisition protocols, label noise, and subtle inter-class variability. In chest radiography, these difficulties are compounded by shortcut learning from non-anatomical artifacts and projection variability, which severely undermine generalization. To address these limitations, we propose DINOv3-SAM, a dual-encoder framework that synergistically integrates complementary visual representations. The architecture combines a self-supervised DINOv3 vision transformer, which captures global semantic context, with the Segment Anything Model (SAM) image encoder, which provides anatomy-aware spatial features. The two feature streams are spatially aligned and adaptively refined through a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM), which emphasizes informative channels and diagnostically relevant regions prior to classification. Notably, only the final DINOv3 layers are fine-tuned while SAM remains frozen, yielding a computationally efficient framework with only 5.3 million trainable parameters. We evaluate DINOv3-SAM across five public datasets spanning diverse modalities and diagnostic tasks: pediatric pneumonia classification, cardiomegaly detection, large-scale RSNA pneumonia detection, COVID-19 radiography, and dermatological lesion classification. A unified stratified train/validation/test protocol ensures consistent and fair evaluation across both binary and multi-class settings. Each configuration was trained three times with different random seeds, and comprehensive comparisons against reproduced CNN baselines and published state-of-the-art methods, supported by statistical significance testing, demonstrate improvements across most datasets and metrics. The proposed framework achieves a mean accuracy of 94.94% (±3.06) on pediatric pneumonia, 97.24% (±0.77) accuracy (AUC 0.998 ±0.001) on COVID-19 radiography, and a mean AUC of 0.8705 (±0.0445) on the challenging RSNA benchmark. These results underscore the efficacy of fusing self-supervised semantic representations with segmentation-informed anatomical cues to enhance robustness against dataset bias, acquisition variability, and cross-domain shifts. The proposed approach offers a reliable foundation for multi-dataset and multi-modality medical image classification in research-oriented decision-support systems.

articles.title: Integration of weight-bearing computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging for advanced musculoskeletal statistical shape modeling of the foot and ankle.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Statistical shape models (SSMs) from three-dimensional (3D) medical imaging describe morphology variation in normal and pathologic anatomy. Within the foot and ankle, weight-bearing computed tomography (WBCT) is used to characterize skeletal deformity but poorly visualizes soft tissue. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides improved evaluation of soft tissue structures but less accurate bone visualization. This methodologic analysis describes and tests reliability of a novel process to generate SSMs from coregistered MRI and WBCT structures. This method is illustrated via two example models: a combined musculoskeletal model and a distal tibia growth plate model. METHODS: Bilateral WBCTs and T1-weighted DIXON MRIs of the lower legs were collected from 14 individuals aged 8 to 18 with no prior lower limb surgery in a control group and hereditary neuropathy group. Bones were segmented from WBCT and manually aligned in MRI space. Alignment reliability was evaluated with intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). Six muscles were segmented semi-automatically and the distal tibia growth plate was manually segmented from MRI. Following cropping, size normalization, and alignment multi-domain SSMs were generated. SSMs were evaluated qualitatively through comparison with expected anatomy and quantitively by calculation of compactness, generalization, and specificity. RESULTS: The alignment method demonstrated excellent reliability with an intrarater ICC of 1 and interrater ICC of 0.999. The musculoskeletal model demonstrated expected atrophy in neuromuscular disease and the preliminary growth plate model showed variation in metaphyseal thickness. Both models demonstrated compactness, specificity, and generalization comparable to published SSMs, requiring 11 and 12 modes to account for 95% of population variance. CONCLUSION: This method allows for application of shape modeling to novel questions in musculoskeletal morphology through simultaneous modeling of bone and soft tissue anatomy. Limitations include manual registration and MRI resolution. This analysis presented examples of muscle and growth plate models, but has broader applications in musculoskeletal analysis.
articles.journal: Int J Comput Assist Radiol Surg

articles.title: Dedicated Versus Generic ePTFE-covered Stent-grafts for Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt in Decompensated Cirrhosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Overt Hepatic Encephalopathy and Shunt Dysfunction.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To estimate the pooled sub-distribution hazard ratio (sHR) of overt hepatic encephalopathy (OHE) and shunt dysfunction in patients with decompensated cirrhosis undergoing transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) using dedicated stent‑grafts (DSG) versus generic stent‑grafts (GSG), and to compare their estimated 1-year event risk, relative risk (RR), and risk difference (RD). MATERIALS AND METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, major biomedical databases were searched for retrospective studies including adults with decompensated cirrhosis undergoing TIPS with DSG or GSG. Pooled estimates for sHR, one‑year cumulative incidence, RR, and RD for OHE and shunt dysfunction were calculated. RESULTS: The pooled estimated 1-year event risk of OHE was 14.3% (95% CI: 7.2-26.4%; I2 = 85%) with DSG and 17.4% (95% CI: 8.1-33.4%; I2 = 91%) with GSG, with no significant subgroup difference (p = 0.611). The RR for OHE with DSG versus GSG was 0.81 (95% CI: 0.51-1.28; p = 0.37; I2=55%), the RD was - 0.03 (95% CI: -0.13 to 0.06; p = 0.45; I2 = 82%), and the pooled sHR was 0.69 (95% CI: 0.13-3.66; p = 0.44; I2 = 78%), none reaching statistical significance. The estimated 1-year event risk of shunt dysfunction was 5.2% (95% CI: 2.6-10.2%; I2 = 63%) with DSG and 10.7% (95% CI: 7.8-14.7%; I2 = 39%) with GSG, with no significant subgroup difference (p = 0.080). DSG was associated with lower shunt dysfunction risk, with RR 0.41 (95% CI: 0.26-0.66; p = 0.0002; I2 = 0%), RD - 0.06 (95% CI: - 0.09 to - 0.03; p < 0.0001; I2 = 0%), and sHR 0.32 (95% CI: 0.17-0.59; p < 0.02; I2 = 0%). CONCLUSION: DSG use in TIPS was associated with significantly lower shunt dysfunction risk compared with GSG, while OHE risk does not differ between stent types. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Grade 3.

articles.title: Association of Capsular Involvement with Delayed Re-intervention After Splenic Artery Embolization for Blunt Splenic Injury.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate whether splenic capsule involvement is associated with delayed re-intervention after splenic artery embolization for blunt splenic injury. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 329 consecutive patients undergoing splenic artery embolization for blunt splenic injury (2017-2025). Capsule involvement was defined as a laceration reaching the splenic surface with capsular disruption or communication with the perisplenic space on contrast-enhanced computed tomography. The primary outcome was delayed re-intervention. Cox and Firth regression were performed, with interobserver agreement assessed by Cohen's kappa. RESULTS: Delayed re-intervention occurred in 26 patients (7.9%) at a median of 6 days; all underwent repeat embolization; none required splenectomy. Twenty (76.9%) were detected on routine surveillance computed tomography without preceding deterioration. Capsule involvement was present in 25 of 26 events. Initial computed tomography showed vascular injury elsewhere in 25 of 26 patients, but neither computed tomography nor angiography showed pseudoaneurysm or active bleeding at the eventual lesion site. Re-intervention occurred in 25 of 245 patients with capsule involvement (10.2%) versus 1 of 84 without (1.2%). Capsule involvement was associated with re-intervention (hazard ratio, 6.82; 95% confidence interval, 1.62-28.74; p = 0.009), but significance was lost after reclassifying two events. Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value were 96.2%, 27.4%, 10.2%, and 98.8%; pre-consensus agreement was 97.6% (Cohen's kappa = 0.938). CONCLUSION: Capsule involvement was associated with delayed re-intervention, but the estimate was statistically fragile because only one capsule-negative event occurred. Surveillance-driven, single-center findings are exploratory; external validation is required before changes in surveillance practice. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 3, prognostic study.

articles.title: Feasibility and Efficacy of Cryoablation as an Eyeball Salvage Therapy for Radiation-resistant Orbital/Choroidal Metastases.
articles.abstract: Orbital and choroidal metastases are rare and usually occur in disseminated disease. Treatment is palliative and aims to preserve visual function and maximize quality of life. When lesions progress despite radiotherapy, enucleation may become necessary, with major functional and psychological consequences. Cryoablation has been used in intraocular tumors such as retinoblastoma, but its use for orbital and choroidal metastases is rarely reported. We describe two patients in whom cryoablation was used as a minimally invasive, eye-preserving alternative to enucleation.
