articles.title: Uterine Artery Embolization for Postpartum Hemorrhage: A 5-Year Single-Center Experience with Emphasis on Embolization Technique and Factors Associated with Clinical Failure.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To describe the embolization technique and clinical outcomes of uterine artery embolization (UAE) for refractory postpartum hemorrhage (PPH), and to identify variables associated with clinical failure. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 150 consecutive patients who underwent UAE for PPH at a single tertiary center (2021-2025). Clinical failure was defined as hysterectomy or repeat embolization (≥ 2 sessions). Variables associated with clinical failure were identified by univariable logistic regression and Fisher's exact test; pre-UAE transfusion was analyzed separately to assess reverse causality. RESULTS: Clinical success was achieved in 140/150 patients (93.3%); clinical failure occurred in 10/150 (6.7%), comprising hysterectomy in 4/10 and repeat embolization in 6/10. Uterine atony was the most common etiology (107/150, 71.3%). Additional vessel embolization was required in 47/150 patients (31.3%). In an exploratory subgroup analysis, emergency cesarean section had a higher failure rate than elective cesarean Sect. (5/32, 15.6% vs. 1/56, 1.8%; p = 0.022). On univariable analysis, higher total pRBC transfusion (OR 1.144; p = 0.003) and lower platelet count (OR 0.982; p = 0.023) were associated with clinical failure; pre-UAE transfusion was not (OR 1.168; p = 0.161), suggesting total pRBC reflects hemorrhage burden rather than antecedent risk. CONCLUSION: UAE achieved clinical success in 140/150 patients (93.3%); additional vessel embolization was required in 47/150 (31.3%). Total pRBC transfusion and platelet count were associated with clinical failure in univariable analysis; procedural variables were not. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 4, Case Series.

articles.title: Feasibility of real-time 1.5-T MR-guided percutaneous irreversible electroporation in a porcine model.
articles.abstract: This exploratory study assessed the procedural feasibility of in‑bore, real‑time magnetic resonance (MR)‑guided percutaneous irreversible electroporation (IRE) using a clinical 1.5-T system in a porcine model. Three healthy anesthetized juvenile swine underwent IRE in normal renal tissue using a prototype pulse generator and MR-conditional coaxial cannula as electrodes. One swine was ablated twice in the same kidney, resulting in statistically non-independent data. The procedure was guided by a balanced steady-state free precession sequence with orthogonal slices and intermittent position verifications using a radial three-dimensional gradient-echo sequence. Preprocedure radiofrequency noise and signal-to-noise ratio measurements showed slightly increased noise levels in generator standby mode without apparent imaging artifacts. Median procedure time was 48 min with an interquartile range of 17 min. Four hours post-procedure, the treatment zone appeared T1-hypointense in delayed contrast-enhanced imaging. For one treatment zone, hematoxylin and eosin staining (H&E), fluorescent terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase-mediated dUTP nick-end labeling staining (TUNEL), and coregistration to MR imaging were performed. H&E showed minor hemorrhaging at the site of electrode insertion. TUNEL demonstrated a strong TUNEL-positive signal correlating with the T1-hypointense signal in delayed contrast-enhanced imaging, with a Dice-Sørensen coefficient of 67%. These findings demonstrate the procedural feasibility of MR-guided percutaneous IRE in clinical 1.5-T MR systems. KEY POINTS: Question Can MR-guided percutaneous irreversible electroporation be performed in a porcine model despite the lack of MR-compliant devices? Findings In four irreversible electroporation procedures in three juvenile pigs, electrodes were successfully placed in the kidney using real-time guidance in a clinical 1.5-T scanner. Relevance statement Real-time MR-guided percutaneous irreversible electroporation is procedurally feasible in a clinical 1.5-T MRI environment, while preserving image quality and enabling arbitrary slice positioning. Further research is required to confirm the reproducibility and enable the translation to oncological applications.

articles.title: Cancer-induced changes in systemic intravascular monocyte dynamics revealed by MRI single cell tracking in a murine breast cancer model.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: In cancer, monocytes with patrolling-like behavior have been associated with antitumoral effects, but their intravascular motion is currently concealed to noninvasive imaging techniques. This study aimed to evaluate systemic monocyte intravascular patrolling-like behavior during tumor growth, immunotherapy, and splenectomy, using single-cell tracking with preclinical time-lapse brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). MATERIALS AND METHODS: In a murine syngeneic breast cancer model (4T1, 67NR), time-lapse MRI (repetitive T2*-weighted gradient-echo sequence after in vivo labeling with iron oxide nanoparticles for monocyte detection) of the brain was conducted using a 9.4 T small animal MRI. Control mice were either naive or received sham injections. Additionally, time-lapse MRI was conducted during immunotherapy or following splenectomy in tumor-bearing and tumor-free mice. Individual cells were identified as hypointensities. Tumors were harvested for ex vivo analysis. RESULTS: The number of detected cells within the brain, distant from the tumor, changed during cancer growth. The cell count was significantly lower for tumor-bearing mice compared to controls. In mice bearing 4T1 tumors, the cell count was significantly lower on day 1 and 9 compared to mice bearing 67NR tumors. During immunotherapy, the monocyte count was significantly lower compared to control, but only in the presence of a tumor. Splenectomy reduced the tumor-associated effect on monocyte dynamics in both low- and highly malignant tumors. CONCLUSION: Based on an exemplary murine breast cancer model, both cancer and immunotherapy change systemic intravascular monocyte patrolling-like behavior early during tumor growth distant from the tumor, an observation that is dependent on the grade of malignancy and the presence of splenic reservoirs. KEY POINTS: Question Do tumors alter systemic intravascular monocyte dynamics during tumor growth, immunotherapy, and splenectomy at distant sites, and can such changes be detected noninvasively? Findings In murine breast cancer, time-lapse MRI revealed reduced monocyte patrolling-like behavior during tumor growth and immunotherapy, influenced by malignancy grade and splenic reservoirs. Critical Relevance Noninvasive single-cell MRI tracking provides novel insights into systemic immune dynamics in cancer, potentially enabling future monitoring of tumor-immune interactions, therapeutic responses, and immune modulation beyond conventional assessment of tumor burden or tumor microenvironment composition.

articles.title: Time-dependent diffusion MRI in determining mismatch repair status of endometrial cancer.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Mismatch repair (MMR) proteins are important in determining therapeutic strategy in endometrial cancer (EC). We investigated the role of microstructural parameters derived from time-dependent diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (td-dMRI) in differentiating MMR status of EC. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective single-center study enrolled patients with suspected EC who underwent preoperative td-dMRI. Tumors were classified as MMR-deficient (dMMR) and MMR-proficient (pMMR) by immunohistochemistry. The microstructural parameters, including intracellular volume fraction (  v i n   ), cell diameter ( d ), cellularity ( ρ ), extracellular diffusivity (  D e x   ), and water exchange rate constant (  k i n   ), were derived by fitting td-dMRI data with three methods (IMPULSED, JOINT, and EXCHANGE), together with the apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC). Differences in these microstructural parameters between dMMR and pMMR EC were compared. The diagnostic performances were evaluated by the areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). RESULTS: Eighty-two patients (17 dMMR, 61.8 ± 10.1 years and 65 pMMR, 58.6 ± 11.8 years) were recruited. dMMR EC exhibited higher  v i n   , ρ and lower  D e x   , ADC values than pMMR EC (p ≤ 0.003). IMPULSED and JOINT demonstrated higher AUCs than conventional ADC (p = 0.025 and 0.046, respectively). The combined selected microstructural parameters (  v in   and  D e x   ) derived from JOINT achieved an AUC of 0.903; JOINT demonstrated superior parametric stability and marginally better calibration than IMPULSED. CONCLUSION: In this exploratory study, td-dMRI discriminated between dMMR and pMMR ECs, providing information on the intricate microscopic organizational structures in tumors. The microstructural parameters may serve as a promising method to improve the diagnostic efficacy of diffusion-weighted MRI in differentiating MMR status of EC. KEY POINTS: Question There remains an unmet need for noninvasive, preoperative tools to assess DNA MMR status in EC. Findings td-dMRI showed significant differences in microstructural parameters between dMMR and pMMR tumors. Relevance statement td-dMRI shows potential as a noninvasive imaging approach for preoperative assessment of MMR status in EC and may support individualized treatment planning.

articles.title: Dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI and tumor microenvironment in hepatocellular carcinoma: exploratory analysis of CD3 + TILs, PD-L1, and glypican-3.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the clinical diagnostic standard in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but its association with the tumor microenvironment is not fully characterized. In this study, we investigated correlations between DCE-MRI parameters and immunohistochemistry features of HCC. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Forty patients, six women and 34 men aged 61.5 ± 10.1 years (mean ± standard deviation) with histologically confirmed HCC were included. DCE-MRI with Gd-EOB-DTPA was performed before surgery, and quantitative parameters were calculated to reflect arterial wash-in, portal venous wash-out and hepatobiliary uptake. Pathological specimens were analyzed for programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1), glypican-3, CD3+ tumor- and stromal-infiltrating lymphocytes, CD68 and CD34. RESULTS: CD3+ stromal lymphocytes infiltration was inversely correlated with the arterial wash-in (r = -0.47; adjusted p-value = 0.025) and several post-arterial parameters. For the other TME components, only exploratory correlations were identified, none of which were statistically significant after adjustment for multiple testing. CD3+ tumoral infiltration lymphocytes with arterial wash-in (r = -0.35) and transitional phase relative signal intensity (SI) (r = 0.35). Native SI was inversely correlated with PD-L1 (r = -0.32). Difference in SI between the transitional and portal phase correlated with glypican-3 expression (r = 0.32). CONCLUSION: DCE-MRI shows a moderate association with stromal infiltrating lymphocytes (CD3⁺ SIL) in HCC. Associations with other components of the TME, including tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (CD3⁺ TIL), PD-L1 and Glypican-3 expression, were observed at uncorrected thresholds, but did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple testing. KEY POINTS: Question DCE-MRI constitutes the cornerstone of HCC diagnosis. Is quantitative assessment of wash-in, wash-out and hepatobiliary uptake associated with non-invasive characterization of the TME? Findings CD3⁺ SIL were associated with tumor wash-in and wash-out parameters. Exploratory associations involving CD3⁺ TIL, PD-L1, and glypican-3 lost significance after multiple-testing adjustment. Relevance statement Quantitative DCE-MRI parameters may provide additional non-invasive information regarding tumor tissue characteristics and the tumor microenvironment of HCC.

articles.title: Patient-specific biophysical AI-powered modeling for predicting RFA volumes in HCC.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To clinically evaluate a fully automated, artificial intelligence-powered, patient-specific biophysical model for predicting radiofrequency ablation (RFA) volumes in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and to compare its performance with manufacturer-provided ablation estimates. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 96 RFA procedures in 65 HCC patients treated using a single ablation with a cluster needle. Tumors, needle position, and postablation zone were manually segmented on periprocedural computed tomography. Liver parenchyma and vascular structures were automatically extracted using deep learning. A graphics processing unit (GPU)-accelerated biophysical model simulated heat transfer, vascular heat-sink effects, and tissue necrosis using patient-specific anatomy and procedural data. Correlations between ablation volume manually segmented and clinical or anatomical parameters (ablation time, ablation tip temperature, tumor-capsule distance, vessel proximity, type, and diameter) were assessed. Model-predicted volumes were compared with ground truth and manufacturer estimates using relative volume difference (RVD) and volume similarity. RESULTS: Final ablation volumes showed wide variability (7.9-78.8 cm³) and were not correlated with any individual clinical or anatomical parameter (Pearson r - 0.02 to 0.29). Across 94 evaluable cases, simulated and ground-truth volumes were similar (p = 0.165), while manufacturer estimates significantly overestimated ablation volume (p < 0.001). The model achieved a median RVD of 0.39 (interquartile range 0.24-0.57), significantly lower than the manufacturer's algorithm (1.04; 0.64-1.61). Incorporating patient-specific ablation time further improved accuracy. Simulation was fast (0.45 s per second of ablation on GPU). CONCLUSION: A fully automated, patient-specific biophysical model substantially improves RFA ablation volume prediction in HCC compared with manufacturer approximations, supporting its potential role in personalized treatment planning and outcome standardization. KEY POINTS: Question In patients with hepatocellular carcinoma, can a fully automated, AI-powered, patient-specific biophysical model predict radiofrequency ablation volume more accurately than manufacturer-provided estimates? Findings A fully automated, AI-powered biophysical model integrating patient-specific anatomy and vasculature predicted RFA volume significantly better than manufacturer estimates (median relative volume difference (RVD) 0.39 versus 1.04). Relevance statement Accurate ablation volume prediction could support personalized radiofrequency ablation (RFA) planning, reduce reliance on operator experience, and standardize treatment margins in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), potentially improving local tumor control and reducing recurrence in cirrhotic patients undergoing thermal ablation.

articles.title: Interaction Between Previous Cesarean Delivery and Anterior Placental Location in Persistent Low-Positioned Placenta: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the interaction between previous Cesarean delivery and anterior placental location in persistent low-positioned placenta and the association between placental edge-to-internal-os distance and persistence among women with a low-lying placenta. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 1508 singleton pregnancies with a low-positioned placenta identified during routine mid-trimester fetal ultrasound between 2020 and 2024. Multivariable analysis was used to evaluate factors associated with persistence and the interaction between previous Cesarean delivery and anterior placental location. Among women with a low-lying placenta, the association between placental edge-to-internal-os distance and persistence was also assessed. RESULTS: Previous Cesarean delivery and anterior placental location interacted significantly in relation to persistent low-positioned placenta (P for interaction = 0.003). The additive interaction risk difference was 20.0 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], 8.2-31.7). Placenta previa at the mid-trimester examination was associated with a higher risk of persistence than low-lying placenta (adjusted relative risk, 5.87; 95% CI, 4.95-6.96). Among women with a low-lying placenta, each 5-mm decrease in placental edge-to-internal-os distance was associated with a 63% higher risk of persistence (adjusted relative risk, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.45-1.83). CONCLUSIONS: Previous Cesarean delivery and anterior placental location interacted significantly in relation to persistent low-positioned placenta, and women with both factors present may warrant closer attention during follow-up. Considering these factors together with the type of low-positioned placenta and placental edge-to-internal-os distance may help refine risk assessment and inform subsequent ultrasound follow-up and clinical management.

articles.title: Diagnostic Value, Sonographic Features, and Factors Associated with Misdiagnosis by Color Doppler Ultrasound for Abdominal Aortic Pseudoaneurysms in Patients With Abdominal Aortic Aneurysmal Dilatation.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the clinical, anatomical, and sonographic features of abdominal aortic pseudoaneurysms (AAP), evaluate the real-world diagnostic performance of color Doppler ultrasound for AAP in patients with abdominal aortic aneurysmal dilatation, and analyze factors associated with misdiagnosis. METHODS: This single-center retrospective diagnostic accuracy study followed STARD 2015. We included 520 consecutive patients with abdominal aortic aneurysmal dilatation detected by color Doppler ultrasound between January 2018 and January 2025. Using surgical findings, computed tomography angiography, or magnetic resonance angiography as the reference standard, we analyzed AAP features, evaluated ultrasound diagnostic performance, and reviewed misdiagnosed cases. RESULTS: A total of 393 patients were included, 25 (6.36%) were confirmed as AAP. Focal wall disruption most frequently occurred in the distal abdominal aorta (64.00%), predominantly on the left and posterior walls. Abdominal or back pain was the most common presenting symptom, with 76.00% of patients having elevated D-dimer levels. The characteristic sonographic findings of AAP were focal aortic wall disruption with a cystic lesion communicating with the aortic lumen. Ultrasound demonstrated 84.00% sensitivity (95% CI: 63.92-95.46), 100.00% specificity (95% CI: 99.00-100.00), and 98.98% overall accuracy (95% CI: 97.41-99.72). In all correctly diagnosed cases, the site of focal wall disruption was 100% concordant with the reference standard. Four cases (16.00%) were misdiagnosed as eccentric true abdominal aortic aneurysms. A retrospective imaging review revealed that these misdiagnoses may be associated with three imaging findings: broad focal wall disruption with absent neck, secondary loss of the typical pseudoaneurysmal to-and-fro flow signature, and coverage of the focal wall disruption by organized thrombus. CONCLUSIONS: Color Doppler ultrasound demonstrates favorable diagnostic performance for AAP in real-world clinical practice and can serve as a reliable first-line non-invasive modality for early screening and diagnosis. Recognition of characteristic features and avoidance of common diagnostic pitfalls can further improve diagnostic accuracy.

articles.title: Magnetic resonance imaging proton density fat fraction and selected quantitative ultrasound methods for hepatic steatosis: histology-referenced diagnostic performance and longitudinal responsiveness-a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To synthesize histology-referenced diagnostic performance at study-selected thresholds and the longitudinal responsiveness of magnetic resonance imaging proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) and selected quantitative ultrasound methods in adults with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease/metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. METHODS: Four databases were searched from database inception through July 1, 2026. Sensitivity, specificity, and odds ratios were pooled with 95% confidence intervals using heterogeneity-selected fixed- or random-effects models. Small-study effects were assessed using funnel plots and Begg tests; longitudinal changes were pooled when change-score standard deviations were reported. RESULTS: In total, 44 articles were included: 34 contributed histology-referenced diagnostic data, and 11 were assessed for longitudinal responsiveness, with 1 article contributing to both. At steatosis grade (S) ≥ 1/S ≥ 2/S ≥3, MRI-PDFF sensitivity and specificity was 93.6%/81.5%/83.1% and 87.1%/86.7%/83.2%, respectively; the controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) was 86.8%/81.2%/86.4% and 98.9%/71.0%/64.6%, respectively. The attenuation coefficient/attenuation imaging sensitivity/specificity was 83.2%/98.1%, 86.4%/79.9%, and 99.3%/76.4%, respectively. Ultrasound-guided attenuation parameter and ultrasound-derived fat fraction evidence was limited. Three head-to-head longitudinal studies included 298 participants, of whom only 158 had analyzable change-score data; in these, pooled changes were -4.53 percentage points for MRI-PDFF and -12.71 dB/m for the CAP. Thirty-two of the 34 diagnostic studies were at high-risk of bias from cohort-selected thresholds. Begg tests did not detect significant small-study effects, although their power was very limited in analyses that included only 2 or 3 studies. CONCLUSION: At study-selected thresholds, MRI-PDFF showed balanced sensitivity and specificity across steatosis grades, whereas quantitative ultrasound varied by method, platform, and threshold. These findings support comparative synthesis but do not establish validated cut-offs or superiority of either modality. CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: Study-selected thresholds limit clinical translation. MRI-PDFF proton density fat fraction and quantitative ultrasound are complementary, with use depending on clinical purpose, platform, and precision needs.

articles.title: Ordinal uncertainty grading in chest radiograph reports using large language models: a REFINE-aligned feasibility and methodology study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Radiologists differ in how strongly they hedge. We tested whether large language models can grade linguistic uncertainty in chest radiograph reports on a 0-3 scale and whether aggregate agreement conceals category-specific differences. METHODS: We used 3,927 public chest radiograph reports (Open-I, Indiana University). Three radiologists independently scored 100 reports from 0 (definitive wording) to 3 (extensive ambiguity). Majority vote, with prespecified attending adjudication for seven complete three-way disagreements, formed the reference standard. Claude Opus 4.5 and Gemini 2.5 Pro scored the same reports from a fixed prompt without task-specific training. We measured agreement using Cohen's quadratic weighted kappa (QWK). We also recorded per-score recall, ordinal error, prompt and reference-standard robustness, and comparison with a keyword-counting baseline. We then scored the remaining 3,827 reports with both models. RESULTS: Human pairwise QWK ranged from 0.421 to 0.659. Claude and Gemini had similar aggregate agreement: QWK: 0.807 [95% confidence interval (CI), 0.722-0.876] and 0.814 (95% CI, 0.735-0.877), respectively; paired difference: 0.007 (95% CI, -0.062 to 0.079). In this validation sample, Claude identified 5/8 reports exactly as Score 3 and Gemini 1/8; Score-3 precision was 5/11 and 1/3, respectively. Of Gemini's seven exact Score-3 misses, six were assigned the adjacent Score 2 category. Reference-standard sensitivities yielded QWK: 0.810-0.841; prompt-variant pairwise agreement ranged from 0.818 to 0.913; repeat runs were identical for 29/30 Claude and 28/30 Gemini reports. All 3,827 Gemini discovery requests completed successfully, with token accounting recorded for the discovery cohort. CONCLUSION: The approach is workable at the corpus scale, but similar aggregate agreement concealed differences in exact Score-3 classification, largely involving the Score-2/3 boundary. The score reflects wording, not clinical risk, and must not be used for risk triage. Clinical or large-scale use requires external validation enriched for ambiguous cases and prior radiologist calibration. CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: These scores may help radiologists audit reporting language and build balanced research evaluation sets, but downstream benefit must be demonstrated rather than assumed.

articles.title: Enterocolitis: a diagnosis in the news that may become more common in the emergency room.
articles.abstract: Foodborne illness affects an estimated 48 million people in the United States each year, and outbreaks peak in the summer. Recalls during the summer of 2026 involved eggs, jalapeños, and frozen blueberries, along with a Cyclospora outbreak traced to iceberg lettuce that caused more than 12,000 illnesses and over 550 hospitalizations. Furthermore, they caused nationwide public anxiety and dominated news headlines. Patients with enteric infection usually reach the emergency department with abdominal pain, and radiologists often read their CT before stool studies return or before anyone suspects infection. This review describes the CT findings of bacterial and parasitic enteritis and colitis. Common features include symmetric segmental or diffuse bowel wall thickening with submucosal edema, mucosal hyperenhancement producing a halo or target pattern, associated fat stranding, engorged mesenteric vessels, and lymphadenopathy. CT also shows complications including toxic megacolon, perforation, and abscess. Recognition of these findings supports timely diagnosis and appropriate management of infectious enterocolitis.
